l4_steps.name: Collect Market Demand Signals
l4_steps.input: Historical booking data, OAG traffic stats, O&D demand reports
l4_steps.output: Demand signal matrix by market/season
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥92%
l4_steps.pain_point: Demand data lags 6-8 weeks; seasonal spikes under-estimated in LF markets

l4_steps.name: Benchmark Competitor Schedules
l4_steps.input: Competitor SSIM files, OAG flight data
l4_steps.output: Competitive gap analysis by route
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage gap identified per route <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Competitor schedule changes filed late; OAG refresh lag causes stale data

l4_steps.name: Review Prior-Season Performance
l4_steps.input: Prior PDEW actuals, load factor by flight, revenue per ASM
l4_steps.output: Season performance scorecard
l4_steps.kpi: Load factor target ≥83%, yield degradation <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point metrics mask connection flow; no codeshare data available

l4_steps.name: Define Season Boundary Dates
l4_steps.input: IATA season schedule, slot deadlines, bank holiday calendars
l4_steps.output: Season start/end dates + IATA submission calendar
l4_steps.kpi: On-time IATA SSIM submission 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA deadlines compress planning window; US holiday variance requires manual overrides

l4_steps.name: Build Draft Flight Schedule
l4_steps.input: Demand matrix, fleet availability plan, crew contract minimums
l4_steps.output: Draft SSIM schedule file with estimated utilisation
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft utilisation ≥13 block hours/day
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual conflict resolution for shared-gate airports; SkyWORKS UI limits batch-edit

l4_steps.name: Run Network Simulation
l4_steps.input: Draft SSIM, O&D demand, fare levels
l4_steps.output: Projected PDEW, RASM, connection flows by scenario
l4_steps.kpi: RASM scenario delta <3% vs baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulation run time 4-6 hours; limits iterative testing cycles in compressed window

l4_steps.name: Optimise Fleet Assignment
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, fleet availability, maintenance windows
l4_steps.output: Fleet assignment plan: tail type per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet conflict rate <1% of rotations
l4_steps.pain_point: Single fleet type (737 family) means AD groundings affect 100% of network simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Validate Crew Legal Compliance
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment, FAR Part 117 rest rules, union CBA minimums
l4_steps.output: Crew feasibility report; flagged violations
l4_steps.kpi: 0 FAR Part 117 violations in final schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew positioning across 8 focus cities constrained; AWS system still stabilising post-Dec 2022 rebuild

l4_steps.name: Check Gate & Slot Availability
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, airport slot files, gate lease agreements
l4_steps.output: Gate conflict report; slot confirmation list
l4_steps.kpi: Gate conflict resolution rate 100% before publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot-controlled airports (LGA, DCA, ORD) require separate coordination thread not integrated in SkyWORKS

l4_steps.name: Revenue Management Alignment Review
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, fare basis files, historical close-in yield data
l4_steps.output: RM-approved schedule with fare class recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Projected revenue within 2% of RM target per route
l4_steps.pain_point: Open boarding policy prevents seat-level RM; NRM implemented 2023, limited historical calibration data

l4_steps.name: Operations Control Sign-Off
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, turn time analysis, ground time buffers
l4_steps.output: Ops-approved schedule with buffer recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: On-time performance (D0) target ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Insufficient turn buffers at focus cities during peak — root cause of Dec 2022 cascade; mandatory 15-min buffer now enforced

l4_steps.name: Execute Aircraft-Crew Co-location Cross-Check
l4_steps.input: Fleet rotation plan, crew pairing plan
l4_steps.output: Co-location validation report; flagged mismatches
l4_steps.kpi: 0 aircraft-crew mismatch at T-0
l4_steps.pain_point: This step was absent pre-Dec 2022; now mandatory. AWS ↔ SkyWORKS API integration point is highest-risk interface

l4_steps.name: Finalise SSIM File
l4_steps.input: Approved schedule, all sign-offs
l4_steps.output: Final SSIM file for submission
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM validation errors = 0
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual SSIM field corrections common; no automated SSIM validator integrated in SkyWORKS

l4_steps.name: Submit to IATA & Slot Coordinators
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot portfolio; IATA acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: 100% slot confirmations received before season open
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot portal fragmentation (each airport has own portal); no single submission hub for US domestic carriers

l4_steps.name: Load Schedule to Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Live schedule in reservations system; bookable inventory open
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule load error rate <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa load process requires 48-hour lead; any late schedule changes must go through emergency change protocol

l4_steps.name: Publish to GDS & Direct Channels
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, Southwest.com
l4_steps.input: Altéa live schedule
l4_steps.output: Bookable flights live across all channels
l4_steps.kpi: GDS availability sync within 4 hours of Altéa load
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS cache refresh lag causes brief price/availability discrepancies on channel-switch; SWABIZ corporate portal sync is independent step

l4_steps.name: Ingest Approved Season Schedule
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file from NP-SP-01
l4_steps.output: Schedule loaded into SkyMAX optimisation engine
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of flights ingested without parse error
l4_steps.pain_point: SSIM format version mismatches between SkyWORKS export and SkyMAX import cause periodic re-loads

l4_steps.name: Load Fleet Availability & Maintenance Windows
l4_steps.input: Fleet register, maintenance plan, AOG reserve list
l4_steps.output: Available aircraft pool per date range
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet availability forecast accuracy ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO system API to SkyMAX is custom-built and brittle; maintenance window changes often require manual SkyMAX refresh

l4_steps.name: Run Fleet Assignment Optimisation
l4_steps.input: Schedule, fleet pool, turn constraints, crew ratios
l4_steps.output: Initial fleet assignment: aircraft type per flight leg
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet utilisation ≥13 block hours/day; deadhead cost minimised
l4_steps.pain_point: Single fleet type removes payload/seat differentiation lever; optimisation is purely rotation-cost and utilisation-based

l4_steps.name: Validate Turn Time Feasibility
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment, ground time per station, gate data
l4_steps.output: Turn time feasibility report; flagged short-turns
l4_steps.kpi: 0 turns below minimum turn time (25 min domestic / 35 min focus city)
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-Dec 2022: minimum turn time floor is now hard-coded constraint. Pre-2022, planners could override — this is now blocked

l4_steps.name: Generate Tail Routing Plan
l4_steps.input: Validated fleet assignment
l4_steps.output: Day-of-week rotation plan: tail number per flight sequence
l4_steps.kpi: Tail routing feasibility 100% (no orphaned tails)
l4_steps.pain_point: 737-700 vs 737-800 capacity difference (143 vs 175) must align with demand forecast by leg — manual override common for thin markets

l4_steps.name: Cross-Check Crew-Aircraft Co-location
l4_steps.input: Tail routing plan, crew pairing plan
l4_steps.output: Co-location validation report
l4_steps.kpi: 0 crew-aircraft positional mismatches at day-start
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS ↔ SkyMAX API integration is the highest-risk interface in the planning stack; mismatch was root cause of Dec 2022 cascade

l4_steps.name: Maintenance Routing Alignment
l4_steps.input: Tail routing plan, scheduled maintenance events
l4_steps.output: Maintenance-aligned routing; tails routed through maintenance bases on correct nights
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of A-checks aligned to correct overnight station
l4_steps.pain_point: Phoenix heavy-check facility (expanded 2024) has limited line maintenance overnight slots; routing must account for bay capacity

l4_steps.name: Stress-Test with IRROP Scenarios
l4_steps.input: Tail routing plan, historical weather/ATC disruption data
l4_steps.output: IRROP resilience score; recovery playbooks per disruption type
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan covers top-10 disruption scenarios; recovery time <3 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Cairo AI tool provides cancellation recommendations in real IRROP but is not integrated into planning-phase stress testing

l4_steps.name: Operations Control Final Approval
l4_steps.input: Stress-tested routing plan, all validation reports
l4_steps.output: Ops-approved tail routing plan
l4_steps.kpi: 0 open conflicts at approval gate
l4_steps.pain_point: VP sign-off is a single point of failure; no documented deputy approval authority

l4_steps.name: Publish Routing to Crew & MRO Systems
l4_steps.system: SkyMAX → Crew Management System (AWS), Custom MRO System
l4_steps.input: Approved tail routing plan
l4_steps.output: Routing published to downstream systems
l4_steps.kpi: Downstream sync confirmed within 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Publish is a multi-system broadcast; AWS and MRO system do not share a common event bus — sequential API calls, no rollback if one fails

l4_steps.name: Archive Plan & Update Capacity Model
l4_steps.input: Final routing plan, utilisation actuals from prior season
l4_steps.output: Archived rotation file; updated capacity baseline model
l4_steps.kpi: Archive latency <24 hours post-season freeze
l4_steps.pain_point: S3 data lake schema changes (12x faster processing post-AWS migration) require periodic re-mapping of archive tooling

l4_steps.name: Extract Booking & Revenue Data by Route
l4_steps.input: PNR booking records, O&D itinerary data, prior 12-month revenue history
l4_steps.output: Route-level revenue dataset by market, cabin, fare family
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction completeness ≥99% of active routes
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D attribution lags 3–5 days; interline revenue excluded from base data, understating true market contribution

l4_steps.name: Pull Ancillary & Fare-Mix Revenue Data
l4_steps.input: Ancillary sales records (bags, seats, upgrades), fare-mix breakdown by RBD
l4_steps.output: Augmented revenue file including total revenue per available seat (RASK) per route
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue captured per departure ≥$18 industry benchmark
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa ancillary attribution is at PNR level, not segment level; multi-leg itineraries require manual pro-ration logic

l4_steps.name: Validate O&D Data Completeness
l4_steps.input: Extracted revenue file, Altéa ancillary data
l4_steps.output: Data quality scorecard; approved dataset or rejection notice
l4_steps.kpi: Data gap rate <1% across all active routes before proceeding
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS Redshift pipeline failures during peak booking windows can delay weekly profitability cycles by 24–48 hours

l4_steps.name: Allocate Direct Operating Costs to Route
l4_steps.input: Fuel burn records, aircraft block hours, crew pay actuals by tail number
l4_steps.output: Direct cost per available seat mile (CASM-direct) per route
l4_steps.kpi: CASM-direct variance vs budget ≤2% per route
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel cost allocation by route requires tail-level tracking; charter and ferry legs inflate CASM if not excluded from scheduled service analysis

l4_steps.name: Apportion Fleet Ownership & Lease Costs
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment records, aircraft lease rates, depreciation schedules from SAP
l4_steps.output: Ownership cost per block hour allocated to each route
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet cost per block hour within ±3% of fleet plan target
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX fleet assignments change frequently intra-day; historical assignment snapshots must be reconciled against actuals to avoid double-counting

l4_steps.name: Assign Airport Fees & Ground Handling Costs
l4_steps.input: Landing fee invoices, ground handling contracts, station cost actuals
l4_steps.output: Station cost per departure allocated to each route
l4_steps.kpi: Station cost recovery rate ≥95% of contracted amounts
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS data is station-level, not route-level; multi-carrier station operations require manual apportionment by frequency share

l4_steps.name: Reconcile & Freeze Route Cost Baseline
l4_steps.input: Direct costs, ownership costs, station costs
l4_steps.output: Total CASM baseline locked for analysis; reconciliation sign-off record
l4_steps.kpi: Cost baseline reconciled within 48 hours of data extraction
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-system reconciliation between SAP, SkyMAX, and SITA AMS requires manual pivot matching; no automated three-way reconciliation tool in place

l4_steps.name: Calculate Route CASM vs RASM Spread
l4_steps.input: Frozen cost baseline, revenue dataset
l4_steps.output: Route P&L margin (RASM minus CASM) ranked by profitability decile
l4_steps.kpi: Network-average RASM–CASM spread ≥1.2¢ per ASM
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM network simulation does not natively integrate SAP cost actuals; finance data must be imported via flat-file, introducing version control risk

l4_steps.name: Benchmark Route Against Network Average
l4_steps.input: Route P&L rankings, competitor schedule and frequency data
l4_steps.output: Competitive context report: market share, frequency parity, fare premium vs peers
l4_steps.kpi: Routes with <80% of network-average margin flagged for review
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data refresh is weekly; fast-moving competitive markets (e.g., ultra-LCC entry) may not be reflected until after analysis is complete

l4_steps.name: Segment Profitability by Season & Day-of-Week
l4_steps.input: Route P&L file, booking curve data segmented by departure date
l4_steps.output: Seasonal P&L heat map per route; peak vs off-peak contribution split
l4_steps.kpi: Seasonal margin variance identified to ±0.5¢ RASM resolution
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM seasonal demand curves are calibrated at the O&D level; thin markets with <200 weekly passengers produce statistically unreliable segmentation outputs

l4_steps.name: Flag Routes Below Profitability Threshold
l4_steps.input: Seasonal P&L heat map, network benchmark data
l4_steps.output: Watch list of underperforming routes requiring scenario modelling
l4_steps.kpi: Routes with RASM–CASM <0.5¢ or negative margin flagged within 5 business days of data freeze
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold calibration is manual; no automated trigger in SkySYM — threshold drift goes undetected between quarterly reviews

l4_steps.name: Model Frequency & Gauge Change Impact
l4_steps.input: Watch-list routes, available aircraft and slot capacity
l4_steps.output: Sensitivity analysis: RASM/CASM delta under ±1 frequency and gauge up/down scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario delta accuracy vs actuals within ±5% on prior test routes
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM gauge scenarios assume average load factor; does not model spill or recapture from competitor capacity dynamically

l4_steps.name: Test Fare Adjustment Recovery Scenarios
l4_steps.input: Route price elasticity curves, current fare ladder, competitor fares from OAG
l4_steps.output: Fare scenario P&L projections; breakeven load factor under revised fare structure
l4_steps.kpi: Projected breakeven LF improvement ≥5pp vs base case to qualify as a viable path
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM elasticity models require ≥18 months of clean booking data; newly launched routes or post-disruption markets produce unreliable elasticity estimates

l4_steps.name: Evaluate Seasonal Suspension Viability
l4_steps.input: Routes with no viable fare/frequency recovery, slot constraints, aircraft redeployment options
l4_steps.output: Suspension impact model: freed capacity redeployment value vs passenger disruption cost
l4_steps.kpi: Redeployment must yield ≥2¢ RASM improvement on receiving route to justify suspension
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX redeployment optimisation does not account for passenger goodwill cost or brand risk on thin community routes serving markets with limited alternatives

l4_steps.name: Prepare Route P&L Recommendation Report
l4_steps.input: Scenario modelling outputs, suspension analysis, competitive benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Executive route P&L report with ranked recommendations (retain/optimise/suspend) and financial impact summary
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered within 5 business days of scenario completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pull from AWS Redshift snapshots; live schedule changes in SkyWORKS during report preparation can make visuals stale before the committee meeting

l4_steps.name: Present Recommendations to Network Investment Committee
l4_steps.input: Route P&L report, scenario models, stakeholder pre-read distributed 48 hours prior
l4_steps.output: Committee decision: approve, revise, or defer each recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of recommendations decided in single committee session without remand
l4_steps.pain_point: Committee decisions require CFO alignment on CASM assumptions; Finance and Network Planning use different cost allocation methodologies, causing recurring meeting delays

l4_steps.name: Implement Approved Schedule Changes
l4_steps.input: Approved committee decisions, SSIM update requirements, slot availability confirmation
l4_steps.output: Updated schedule in SkyWORKS; SSIM filed to GDS and Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule changes published to GDS within 72 hours of committee approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS to Altéa PSS schedule sync failures have occurred during peak filing periods, requiring manual reconciliation that delays booking availability

l4_steps.name: Monitor Post-Action Route Performance
l4_steps.input: Live booking data on modified routes, updated CASM actuals from SAP
l4_steps.output: 30/60/90-day performance tracking report vs projected recovery targets
l4_steps.kpi: RASM–CASM spread on modified routes trending toward target within 60 days
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM monitoring dashboards do not automatically flag when post-action routes underperform vs projection; analyst must manually compare actuals to scenario model each cycle

l4_steps.name: Analyse network demand vs slot inventory
l4_steps.input: O&D demand forecast for target IATA season
l4_steps.output: Airport-level demand vs slot-capacity gap list
l4_steps.kpi: Slot coverage ratio ≥95% of planned frequencies
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand signals do not automatically map to coordinator-level slot granularity; manual crosswalk required for Level 3 airports

l4_steps.name: Prioritise slot request list by route value
l4_steps.input: Demand-gap list; route P&L rankings from prior season
l4_steps.output: Ranked slot request list with commercial priority scores
l4_steps.kpi: Top-20 revenue routes have slot requests filed within 5 days of season open
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS priority ranking may conflict with network-level schedule symmetry goals, requiring manual override

l4_steps.name: Extract historical slot series from IATA CRS
l4_steps.input: Equivalent season data: previous two years of operated series
l4_steps.output: Historical series report with utilisation rate per slot
l4_steps.kpi: Historical utilisation validated for 100% of held series within 3 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA CRS data latency of up to 48 h means late-returned competitor slots are invisible during initial analysis, skewing capacity view

l4_steps.name: Assess 80/20 grandfather rights eligibility
l4_steps.input: Historical series utilisation report
l4_steps.output: Eligibility status per series: protected, at-risk, or lost
l4_steps.kpi: ≥98% of held series retain grandfather status; at-risk flag raised ≥10 weeks before conference
l4_steps.pain_point: Force majeure waiver criteria (e.g. COVID-era precedents) are interpreted inconsistently by airport coordinators, creating approval uncertainty

l4_steps.name: File force majeure exemption for at-risk series
l4_steps.input: At-risk series list; documented operational disruption evidence
l4_steps.output: Exemption submission with supporting evidence package
l4_steps.kpi: Exemption accepted by coordinator within 10 business days for 90% of filings
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinator acceptance rates vary by airport authority; no standardised SLA exists under IATA WSG, exposing series to arbitrary rejection

l4_steps.name: Generate SSIM slot request messages in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Ranked slot request list; confirmed fleet plan
l4_steps.output: SSIM-format Initial Slot Request (ISR) file per coordinated airport
l4_steps.kpi: Zero SSIM format errors on submission; ISR filed ≥8 weeks before IATA slot conference
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS SSIM export does not auto-validate against airport coordinator's declared coordination parameters (declared capacity), requiring manual cross-check

l4_steps.name: Submit Initial Slot Requests to coordinators
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM ISR files
l4_steps.output: Submission receipt and coordinator acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ISRs acknowledged within 48 h of IATA deadline; no late submissions
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple national coordinators (e.g. Heathrow Airport Slots Ltd, DFW, CDG FAB) use non-standard portals alongside SCR, increasing coordination overhead

l4_steps.name: Review coordinator initial allocation returns
l4_steps.input: Coordinator allocation response file (SSIM)
l4_steps.output: Gap analysis: requested vs allocated slots per airport
l4_steps.kpi: Gap analysis completed within 48 h of receiving allocation returns
l4_steps.pain_point: Allocation returns often partially match requests with no rationale, requiring reverse-engineering of coordinator capacity logic using OAG data

l4_steps.name: Prepare slot negotiation brief for conference
l4_steps.input: Gap analysis; competitor schedule data from OAG
l4_steps.output: Negotiation brief: priority gaps, swap targets, walk-away positions
l4_steps.kpi: Brief approved by VP Network Planning ≥5 days before conference
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM simulation does not model competitor reaction to slot swaps, limiting predictive accuracy of negotiation scenarios

l4_steps.name: Attend IATA slot conference and negotiate gaps
l4_steps.input: Negotiation brief; conference room bilateral schedule
l4_steps.output: Agreed slot swaps and bilateral exchange confirmations
l4_steps.kpi: ≥75% of priority gap slots resolved at conference; average delta from preferred time ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines without alliance membership (e.g. unaligned LCCs) have reduced swap leverage at slot conferences; coordinators may favour legacy hub carriers

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved gaps to coordinator appeal panel
l4_steps.input: Unresolved gap list; documented justification
l4_steps.output: Appeal submission; coordinator ruling
l4_steps.kpi: Appeals filed within 24 h of conference close; ruling received within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA World Slot Guidelines appeal process is non-binding; coordinators retain final authority, making outcomes unpredictable for non-dominant carriers

l4_steps.name: Import confirmed slots into SkyWORKS schedule
l4_steps.input: Final confirmed allocation SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Updated master schedule with slot-locked departure/arrival times
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of confirmed slots imported without timing conflict within 2 business days of final allocation
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot times confirmed post-conference may conflict with crew pairing and aircraft routing already modelled in SkyWORKS, requiring full re-optimisation cycle

l4_steps.name: Publish confirmed SSIM to GDS and PSS
l4_steps.input: Slot-locked master schedule
l4_steps.output: SSIM message distributed to Sabre GDS, Amadeus GDS, Travelport GDS, and Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM published within 5 business days of slot confirmation; GDS pick-up error rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway does not automatically ingest SSIM updates; NDC-sourced content requires separate manual schedule push, risking content divergence

l4_steps.name: Monitor weekly slot utilisation against 80% rule
l4_steps.input: Operated flight departure reports; slot series holdings
l4_steps.output: Weekly utilisation dashboard: series compliance status
l4_steps.kpi: Utilisation ≥80% maintained for all series; alerts triggered if any series falls below 85% buffer
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa operational departure data lags coordinator reporting window by up to 72 h, creating risk of under-reporting in close-to-threshold series

l4_steps.name: Return or swap underutilised slots to coordinator
l4_steps.input: Underutilised series flagged below 85% buffer
l4_steps.output: Slot return notification or swap offer filed with coordinator
l4_steps.kpi: Returns filed ≥6 weeks before operated date; 100% of below-threshold series actioned within 48 h of flag
l4_steps.pain_point: Late slot returns reduce secondary market swap opportunities; airlines that pool returns informally (Star Alliance, oneworld) gain competitive advantage unavailable to unaligned carriers

l4_steps.name: Archive season compliance evidence for grandfather rights
l4_steps.input: Full-season utilisation records; exemption filings; coordinator correspondence
l4_steps.output: Compliance evidence archive; grandfather rights assertion package for next equivalent season
l4_steps.kpi: Archive complete within 10 business days of season end; 100% of series have supporting evidence on record
l4_steps.pain_point: No industry-standard digital audit trail format exists; evidence quality varies by coordinator, creating litigation risk if grandfather rights are disputed

l4_steps.name: Identify codeshare & interline partner candidates
l4_steps.input: Network gap analysis, O&D demand data, commercial strategy brief
l4_steps.output: Ranked partner shortlist with O&D overlap scores
l4_steps.kpi: Min 5 candidate partners assessed per planning cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data latency (updated weekly) may miss recent partner schedule changes; analysts must cross-check with SSIM direct feeds

l4_steps.name: Analyse partner O&D network overlap and revenue potential
l4_steps.input: Partner SSIM schedule, OAG market share data, own O&D traffic database
l4_steps.output: Revenue opportunity model: incremental pax and yield per route
l4_steps.kpi: Projected incremental load factor contribution ≥3 ppts on thin O&D routes
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D demand models assume point-to-point flows; interline connecting itineraries require manual traffic splitting adjustments

l4_steps.name: Verify IIA and SPA agreement status with legal
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier code, IATA IIA registry extract
l4_steps.output: Agreement status confirmation (IIA active / SPA in place / none)
l4_steps.kpi: Agreement status verified within 2 business days of partner selection
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA IIA registry updates lag actual bilateral negotiations by up to 30 days; expired SPAs may not be flagged in the finance system

l4_steps.name: Request SSIM schedule data feed from partner airline
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier approval, IATA SSIM Chapter 7 format specification
l4_steps.output: Received partner SSIM file imported into SkyWORKS schedule database
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM file received and validated within 5 business days of partner agreement
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-IATA partners (charter, regional) may supply non-standard SSIM variants requiring manual field mapping before SkyWORKS can import

l4_steps.name: Validate connection times against airport MCT tables
l4_steps.input: Partner SSIM flights, own schedule, IATA MCT database per airport
l4_steps.output: MCT compliance report: list of connections meeting/failing minimum connect time
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of proposed connect itineraries MCT-compliant before GDS loading
l4_steps.pain_point: MCT tables vary by terminal and domestic/international split; SkyWORKS uses airport-level MCTs and may not reflect terminal reassignments after gate changes

l4_steps.name: Resolve schedule conflicts via SSIM SCR negotiation
l4_steps.input: MCT non-compliance list, partner contact, SSIM SCR message format
l4_steps.output: Revised partner or own schedule achieving MCT compliance
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule conflicts resolved within 10 business days; <5% of proposed connections requiring rescheduling
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner airlines prioritise own network optimisation; schedule adjustment requests are often rejected or delayed beyond SSIM submission deadlines (D-180)

l4_steps.name: Confirm aligned codeshare schedule and flight numbering
l4_steps.input: MCT-compliant schedule, codeshare designator allocation (IATA two-letter code)
l4_steps.output: Confirmed codeshare flight number series filed in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.kpi: Codeshare flight numbers registered with IATA within 7 days of schedule confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Duplicate flight number conflicts with own metal flights require manual deconfliction; SkyWORKS does not auto-detect cross-carrier designator clashes

l4_steps.name: Configure block-space or free-sale inventory allocation
l4_steps.input: Confirmed codeshare schedule, capacity agreement (block vs free-sale terms)
l4_steps.output: Inventory allocation rules loaded into Altéa PSS for codeshare flight numbers
l4_steps.kpi: Block-space utilisation target ≥70% within 30 days of schedule launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Free-sale arrangements require real-time availability sharing via IATA Type B TELETYPE or PADIS; latency >500ms causes ghost availability in partner booking systems

l4_steps.name: File interline prorate and SPA agreements via ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Bilateral prorate formula, revenue split percentage, SPA effective date
l4_steps.output: Published ATPCO prorate agreement record accessible by all GDS and PSS
l4_steps.kpi: ATPCO filing effective within 24 hours of D-1 activation date; 0 unpriced itineraries at launch

l4_steps.input: Live booking data (Altéa), load factor actuals, OTP data, re-accommodation completion rate

l4_steps.name: Extract historical O&D traffic data

l4_steps.name: Compile and submit commercial committee pack
l4_steps.input: Business case deck, P&L model, ops feasibility sign-off, demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Formal new market entry proposal submitted to Commercial Committee
l4_steps.kpi: Pack submission ≥10 business days before committee review date
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-functional sign-off (Revenue Mgmt, Ops, Finance) often delayed due to differing planning horizons; average pack completion takes 18 days vs. 10-day target

l4_steps.name: File approved schedule and slots in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Commercial Committee approval, proposed SSIM schedule record
l4_steps.output: New market schedule inserted into official season file
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule filed ≥120 days before service start (IATA SSIM standard)
l4_steps.pain_point: Late approvals compress the SSIM filing window, risking GDS distribution gaps and reducing advance booking lead time below optimal 90-day curve

l4_steps.name: Publish new route to GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.input: Approved SSIM schedule, fare filing from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: New route live in Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, and NDC channel
l4_steps.kpi: GDS content live ≥90 days before first departure; NDC content live within 24 hours of GDS
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filing cycle runs twice daily; missed filing window delays public fare availability by up to 12 hours, impacting early adopter bookings on launch-day announcement

l4_steps.name: Scan competitive landscape for partnership gaps
l4_steps.input: Annual network strategy review, O&D demand data, competitor alliance footprint
l4_steps.output: Partnership opportunity heat-map with prioritised O&D pairs
l4_steps.kpi: O&D market coverage gap ≥5% of total addressable revenue identified
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data lags IATA SSIM submissions by 4–6 weeks, causing stale competitive benchmarks during fast-moving alliance negotiations

l4_steps.name: Assess network complementarity of candidate partners
l4_steps.input: Candidate airline schedules (OAG), own network SSIM, O&D demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Network complementarity score and connecting-flow traffic simulation per candidate
l4_steps.kpi: Incremental connecting pax potential ≥50,000 pax/year per candidate to proceed
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM simulation accuracy degrades for thin O&D markets (<10 bookings/day) where demand signal is insufficient for reliable modelling

l4_steps.name: Gate: Approve candidate shortlist for business case
l4_steps.input: Network complementarity scores, SkyCAST demand forecast by O&D
l4_steps.output: Approved shortlist of ≤3 partner candidates for full financial modelling
l4_steps.kpi: Shortlist decision cycle ≤10 business days from scan initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand forecasts for new O&D markets (no historical booking data) carry ±25% confidence intervals, creating executive pushback on go/no-go decisions

l4_steps.name: Model incremental codeshare revenue per O&D
l4_steps.input: Approved partner shortlist, O&D demand forecast, own fare inventory data
l4_steps.output: Revenue uplift model: incremental yield, load factor impact, and fare dilution estimate per O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Projected revenue uplift ≥3% on affected O&D markets within 12 months of go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM O&D revenue attribution for connecting itineraries is split by leg, obscuring true contribution of partner-fed traffic; manual adjustment required

l4_steps.name: Model interline prorate and revenue-share economics
l4_steps.input: Revenue uplift model, proposed prorate split (IATA pro-rata or bilateral rates), partner financial statements
l4_steps.output: NPV analysis and 5-year P&L impact; minimum acceptable prorate floor rate
l4_steps.kpi: Partnership NPV ≥ $5M over 5-year horizon to proceed to regulatory review
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA standard prorate methodology (IATA Resolution 850) frequently under-compensates short-haul feeder partners, leading to prolonged bilateral negotiation cycles averaging 6–9 months

l4_steps.name: Gate: Approve business case for regulatory submission
l4_steps.input: NPV model, revenue uplift forecast, prorate economics, risk register
l4_steps.output: Signed business case approval; mandate for regulatory and legal teams to proceed
l4_steps.kpi: Business case approval decision ≤15 business days from financial model submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Executive approval stalls when NPV is marginal (e.g. $5–8M) and downside scenarios show revenue dilution on own metal — no standardised sensitivity threshold exists

l4_steps.name: File for antitrust immunity or bilateral ASA review
l4_steps.input: Signed business case, proposed route list, partner agreement term sheet
l4_steps.output: DOT antitrust immunity application (US routes) or bilateral ASA amendment filing; IATA CRS slot filing if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory filing submitted within 20 business days of business case approval
l4_steps.pain_point: US DOT antitrust immunity reviews average 12–18 months; EU bilateral amendments require ECAA or bilateral renegotiation via member-state government, adding 6–24 months of uncertainty

l4_steps.name: Assess slot availability at partner hub airports
l4_steps.input: Proposed connecting schedule, partner hub slot pool data, IATA WSG constraints
l4_steps.output: Slot feasibility report; list of required slot swaps or grandfather-right acquisitions
l4_steps.kpi: Required slots secured for ≥90% of planned codeshare frequency within IATA schedule season
l4_steps.pain_point: Level 3 coordinated airports (e.g. LHR, JFK, CDG) have near-zero slot availability; grandfather rights are held by incumbents, making new entry dependent on costly secondary market transactions or seasonal swap negotiations

l4_steps.name: Gate: Confirm regulatory and slot approvals are obtainable
l4_steps.input: Regulatory filing status, slot feasibility report, legal counsel opinion
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision on regulatory path; if no-go, revised route scope or exit recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Clear regulatory pathway confirmed within 30 business days of filing; slot coverage ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory timelines are non-deterministic; slot constraints at Level 3 airports can invalidate the entire business case after 3–6 months of investment, with no partial recovery mechanism

l4_steps.name: Negotiate Interline Traffic Agreement and prorate rates
l4_steps.input: Approved business case, regulatory clearance, IATA prorate methodology benchmark
l4_steps.output: Signed Interline Traffic Agreement (ITA) with bilateral prorate rates; Altéa interline carrier setup request
l4_steps.kpi: ITA negotiation closed within 60 days of regulatory clearance; prorate floor ≥65% of published fare for feeder leg
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa interline carrier onboarding requires manual BSP/clearing house configuration (ARC/IATA) taking 4–8 weeks after ITA signing — creates gap between commercial agreement and operational readiness

l4_steps.name: Negotiate codeshare block-space or free-sale agreement
l4_steps.input: Signed ITA, revenue model (minimum guaranteed block vs free-sale risk), partner capacity plan
l4_steps.output: Signed codeshare agreement specifying seat-block size, free-sale cap, and operating/marketing carrier designations
l4_steps.kpi: Codeshare seat utilisation ≥70% on protected block within 6 months of launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Free-sale agreements create inventory cannibalisation risk when partner's own metal competes on overlapping O&D segments; NRM O&D controls do not natively arbitrate between own-metal and codeshare inventory in real time

l4_steps.name: Gate: Validate agreement terms against revenue policy
l4_steps.input: Signed ITA, codeshare agreement, updated revenue model with final prorate and block-space terms
l4_steps.output: Final commercial approval; instruction to legal to execute agreements and initiate system configuration
l4_steps.kpi: Agreement terms deliver ≥90% of NPV projected in approved business case
l4_steps.pain_point: Late-stage concessions (e.g. prorate adjustments, block-space size reductions) during final negotiation rounds can erode NPV below approval threshold without triggering a formal re-approval cycle

l4_steps.name: File codeshare and interline fares via ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Executed codeshare agreement, joint fare construction rules, partner published fares
l4_steps.output: ATPCO fare filings: through-fares, combinability rules, and ticketing authority records (TAT/TAH)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of planned O&D joint fares live in GDS within 14 days of agreement execution
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing errors in combinability rules (Cat 10) cause GDS repricing failures, leading to customer-facing booking errors and revenue leakage; testing requires manual GDS shop verification across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus

l4_steps.name: Configure PSS codeshare inventory and host carrier setup
l4_steps.input: Signed codeshare agreement, ATPCO fare filings, partner IATA carrier code and BSP enrollment
l4_steps.output: Altéa codeshare host/operating carrier configuration; booking class mapping; through check-in profile
l4_steps.kpi: PSS configuration completed and unit-tested within 21 days of agreement execution
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa codeshare configuration requires coordination across PSS, DCS (Departure Control), and Loyalty modules; misaligned Rapid Rewards/FFP accrual rules on partner segments result in customer complaints and manual points corrections

l4_steps.name: Configure GDS codeshare display and availability feed
l4_steps.input: Altéa codeshare configuration, partner SSIM schedule, ATPCO fare records
l4_steps.output: Codeshare itineraries visible and bookable in Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; NDC API feed updated
l4_steps.kpi: Codeshare itinerary display accuracy ≥99% across all three GDS within 7 days of Altéa config completion
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS display logic for codeshare itineraries varies by channel (Sabre vs Travelport vs Amadeus); duplicate or ghost inventory appears when schedule changes are not propagated simultaneously across all three, requiring manual suppression

l4_steps.name: Gate: Pass end-to-end interoperability test suite
l4_steps.input: PSS and GDS configuration, ATPCO fare records, test booking scripts (≥50 scenarios)
l4_steps.output: Interoperability test report; pass/fail verdict; defect log for remediation
l4_steps.kpi: ≥95% of test scenarios pass (booking, ticketing, check-in, FFP accrual, irregular ops rebooking)
l4_steps.pain_point: Irregular operations (IROPS) rebooking on codeshare itineraries across PSS boundaries is the most common test failure; Altéa does not natively rebook passengers onto partner-operated flights without manual agent intervention

l4_steps.name: Launch codeshare service and activate commercial marketing
l4_steps.input: Passed interoperability test, regulatory approvals confirmed, GDS live
l4_steps.output: Codeshare service live; press release issued; joint marketing campaign activated
l4_steps.kpi: First-week codeshare booking volume ≥50% of 90-day ramp forecast
l4_steps.pain_point: Launch delays caused by late regulatory clearance compress the marketing window before the IATA schedule season, reducing awareness and first-season load factors vs forecast by an average of 8–12 percentage points

l4_steps.name: Monitor connecting yield, load factor, and prorate settlement
l4_steps.input: Daily booking and revenue data from Altéa, GDS booking reports, IATA BSP settlement files
l4_steps.output: Monthly partnership performance dashboard: connecting pax yield, load factor, prorate actuals vs model, ancillary attach rate
l4_steps.kpi: Connecting pax yield ≥80% of model projection; prorate settlement discrepancy ≤2% of billed revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP prorate settlement cycles are monthly with 45-day lag, making real-time revenue performance tracking dependent on booking-level proxies in Redshift rather than actual settled amounts

l4_steps.name: Gate: Annual review — expand, renegotiate, or exit partnership
l4_steps.input: 12-month performance dashboard, updated NPV reforecast, partner relationship assessment, regulatory renewal status
l4_steps.output: Strategic decision: expand routes, renegotiate prorate/block terms, or serve notice of termination per agreement exit clause
l4_steps.kpi: Annual review completed and decision issued ≤90 days before agreement renewal deadline; partnership retained if NPV reforecast ≥80% of original approval threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: Exit clauses in codeshare agreements typically require 6–12 months notice; airlines that miss the review cycle are locked into underperforming partnerships for an additional year, absorbing continued prorate losses

l4_steps.name: Confirm seasonal schedule freeze milestone
l4_steps.input: Seasonal schedule deadline calendar; IATA scheduling conference date
l4_steps.output: Freeze confirmation memo; SkyWORKS workspace locked for SSIM export
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule frozen ≥8 weeks before IATA seasonal deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS freeze locks the shared planning workspace; late changes require an emergency amendment process that triggers full GDS re-distribution

l4_steps.name: Extract full flight schedule from SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Confirmed schedule freeze; all routes with equipment assignments and frequency patterns
l4_steps.output: Raw schedule export file (flights, equipment ICAO codes, times, frequencies, cabin configs)
l4_steps.kpi: Extract completeness ≥99.5% of scheduled flight legs
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS export occasionally omits wet-lease and codeshare-operated segments, requiring manual reconciliation before SSIM generation

l4_steps.name: Validate schedule data completeness and codes
l4_steps.input: Raw schedule export file
l4_steps.output: Validated schedule dataset with exception log of missing or invalid fields
l4_steps.kpi: Data quality score ≥99% (missing or invalid fields <1% of records)
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing IATA airport codes or unrecognised aircraft ICAO type codes cause SSIM Chapter 7 format rejection at downstream GDS ingestion

l4_steps.name: Generate SSIM Chapter 7 format file
l4_steps.input: Validated schedule dataset
l4_steps.output: SSIM Chapter 7 formatted file with header, record types 1–4, and trailer
l4_steps.kpi: File generated within 4 business hours of schedule freeze confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS SSIM output does not include non-IATA member charter operations; manual record append required, increasing error risk

l4_steps.name: Run IATA SSIM syntax and schema validation
l4_steps.input: SSIM Chapter 7 file
l4_steps.output: Validation report: pass/fail status with line-level error list
l4_steps.kpi: Zero critical format errors before external submission
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS embedded IATA SSIM validator version lags IATA annual publication cycle by up to 6 months, causing false positives on new record type extensions requiring manual sign-off

l4_steps.name: Correct SSIM format errors and re-validate
l4_steps.input: Validation error report with line references
l4_steps.output: Corrected and revalidated SSIM file cleared for distribution
l4_steps.kpi: Error resolution cycle completed within 2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Iterative correction loops frequently triggered by aircraft sub-fleet code changes (e.g. 73H vs 73W); no automated mapping maintained between SkyWORKS fleet types and SSIM equipment codes

l4_steps.name: Identify slot-controlled airports in schedule
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM file; IATA Level 2 and Level 3 coordinated airport register
l4_steps.output: Slot request list by airport, season, and designated coordinator body
l4_steps.kpi: Slot request list submitted ≥4 weeks before IATA scheduling conference
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Level 2/3 coordination status changes seasonally with no automated alert; reclassification of an airport discovered post-SSIM generation forces last-minute slot programme additions

l4_steps.name: Submit slot requests to airport coordinators
l4_steps.input: Slot request list; SSIM extract for the relevant airports
l4_steps.output: SLOT/S2 and SAL messages submitted to ACL (UK), COHOR (France), FAA ATCSCC (US), and regional bodies
l4_steps.kpi: Submission acknowledgement received from all coordinators within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Some regional coordinators (e.g. ACNUSA for Paris CDG, NACC for Caribbean) require national-format messages rather than standard IATA WSG SSIM; manual reformatting needed per coordinator

l4_steps.name: Reconcile slot confirmations against requests
l4_steps.input: Coordinator confirmation messages; original slot request register
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation report: confirmed vs. requested vs. denied slots with variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Slot hit rate ≥90% of requested times within ±30 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot denials at Level 3 constrained airports (LHR, JFK, FRA) require re-planning iterations with the Network team; no automated feedback loop into SkyWORKS to propagate confirmed times back to the live schedule

l4_steps.name: Transmit SSIM to Sabre Schedule Distribution
l4_steps.input: Validated and slot-reconciled SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Sabre SDS ingest confirmation receipt with processing timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Sabre display accuracy ≥99% within 48 hours of transmission
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre SDS equipment type mapping for new aircraft variants (e.g. A321XLR, 737 MAX 10) lags IATA SSIM type code releases by up to one schedule season, causing booking class display errors

l4_steps.name: Transmit SSIM to Amadeus and Travelport GDS
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM file
l4_steps.output: GDS ingest confirmation receipts from Amadeus and Travelport
l4_steps.kpi: Display accuracy ≥99% within 48 hours on both GDS platforms
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus and Travelport have different SSIM ingestion cutoff times and batch processing windows; staggered submissions required to avoid inconsistent schedule displays across booking channels during the transition window

l4_steps.name: Distribute schedule data to OAG and Cirium
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM file
l4_steps.output: OAG and Cirium data feed ingest acknowledgements
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule data live on OAG and Cirium within 72 hours of SSIM receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG charges amendment fees for mid-cycle corrections; unplanned network changes require budget pre-approval before re-submission, introducing a 2–5 day delay in schedule visibility for travel agencies and competitors

l4_steps.name: Verify GDS schedule display accuracy post-load
l4_steps.input: Submitted SSIM file; post-load GDS availability and schedule displays
l4_steps.output: Display verification report: error rate by flight, equipment, and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: GDS display error rate <0.5% across sampled flights
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS automated post-load checks do not cover all booking class inheritance mappings for new routes; manual spot-check required for every new city-pair added to the schedule

l4_steps.name: Distribute SSIM to codeshare and interline partners
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM file; interline and codeshare partner agreement register
l4_steps.output: SSIM sub-files transmitted to each codeshare and interline partner via SITA STB
l4_steps.kpi: Partner receipt confirmation received within 48 hours for ≥95% of partners
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA STB acknowledgement messages do not distinguish between received and processed status; partners occasionally load superseded SSIM versions when multiple amendments are in flight simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Notify airports of schedule via IATA AHM 090
l4_steps.input: Final confirmed schedule with slot allocations
l4_steps.output: AHM 090 schedule notification messages transmitted to all served airports
l4_steps.kpi: Airport acknowledgement received from ≥95% of notified airports within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: AHM 090 message format compliance varies by airport handler; some outstations require a direct email supplement alongside SITA MATIP messages, adding manual workload with no audit trail in AMS

l4_steps.name: Archive versioned SSIM with change log
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file; amendment history register
l4_steps.output: Versioned SSIM archive in AWS S3 with structured change log (season, date, amendment number, changed flights)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% version retention; any historical SSIM retrievable within 1 business hour
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated versioning in SkyWORKS SSIM module; manual naming conventions lead to version confusion when multiple mid-season amendments are active, creating audit and regulatory traceability risk

l4_steps.name: Manage mid-season SSIM amendment cycle
l4_steps.input: Network change requests; schedule irregularity reports; commercial re-routing decisions
l4_steps.output: Amendment SSIM file; updated GDS displays; re-notified partners and airports
l4_steps.kpi: Full amendment cycle (generate → validate → distribute → verify) completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-season amendments trigger full re-distribution to all GDS, aggregators, and partners; SkyWORKS SSIM module has no selective-update capability, so even single-flight changes require a complete file re-transmission

l4_steps.name: Initiate seasonal schedule freeze in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Board-approved seasonal schedule (IATA season S26/W26)
l4_steps.output: Frozen schedule record with freeze timestamp and version lock
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule frozen ≥330 days before season start per IATA standard
l4_steps.pain_point: Late commercial decisions (new routes, frequency changes) force freeze date slippage, compressing the GDS loading window and risking incomplete availability at booking opening

l4_steps.name: Validate schedule against airport slot constraints
l4_steps.input: Frozen schedule from SkyWORKS, IATA slot declarations for coordinated airports
l4_steps.output: Slot validation report with conflict flag per airport
l4_steps.kpi: 100% slot compliance achieved before SSIM generation; zero unresolved conflicts at freeze
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot-constrained airports (LHR, JFK, CDG, NRT) require manual bilateral negotiation; automated IATA CRS checks surface conflicts but offer no resolution path, requiring scheduler intervention

l4_steps.name: Resolve slot conflicts and revalidate schedule
l4_steps.input: Slot validation report listing conflicting departure/arrival windows
l4_steps.output: Revised schedule with adjusted slot times, resubmitted to IATA CRS
l4_steps.kpi: Slot conflict resolution within 5 business days of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot swaps require bilateral agreement with competing carriers; absence of a multilateral slot exchange platform means resolution depends on ad-hoc email negotiation with slot coordinators

l4_steps.name: Generate SSIM Chapter 7 file from frozen schedule
l4_steps.input: Validated, slot-compliant frozen schedule
l4_steps.output: SSIM Chapter 7 flat file (.ssim) containing all flight records for the season
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM generated within 2 hours of freeze confirmation; file size validated within expected range
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex codeshare and interline agreements require precise segment-level carrier attribution in SSIM records; errors in marketing vs. operating carrier fields cause booking failures across all GDS channels

l4_steps.name: Validate SSIM file against IATA format standards
l4_steps.input: Generated SSIM Chapter 7 file
l4_steps.output: SSIM validation report detailing field-level errors, warnings, and record counts
l4_steps.kpi: Zero format errors before transmission; validation run completed in <30 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA SSIM Chapter 7 format is field-position-exact; minor field-length violations or non-standard aircraft type codes cause full file rejection by GDS ingest pipelines, requiring a complete regeneration cycle

l4_steps.name: Correct SSIM errors and regenerate file
l4_steps.input: SSIM validation error report with specific record and field references
l4_steps.output: Corrected SSIM file ready for re-validation
l4_steps.kpi: Correction and regeneration cycle completed in ≤4 hours per iteration
l4_steps.pain_point: Root cause of SSIM errors often lies in upstream schedule attributes (equipment codes, operating carrier flags); manual correction risks introducing new errors without an integrated diff-check tool

l4_steps.name: Submit validated SSIM to OAG for GDS distribution
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM Chapter 7 file with zero format errors
l4_steps.output: OAG submission confirmation with distribution ticket ID and estimated processing completion time
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM submitted to OAG ≥12 months before season start for initial seasonal load; re-submissions within 4 hours of correction sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG processing queue can introduce 24–48 hour delays during peak IATA schedule submission periods (March and October); cascading delay compresses the booking-open window for new routes

l4_steps.name: Monitor Sabre GDS schedule ingestion and loading
l4_steps.input: OAG distribution confirmation, Sabre loading status feed
l4_steps.output: Sabre loading confirmation report; discrepancy log if mismatches detected
l4_steps.kpi: Sabre schedule parity ≥99.5% within 72 hours of SSIM submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre's batch processing window is nightly; intraday schedule corrections are not reflected until the following day's run, requiring a manual Sabre support ticket for urgent changes such as flight cancellations or time shifts

l4_steps.name: Monitor Travelport GDS schedule ingestion and loading
l4_steps.input: OAG distribution confirmation, Travelport Apollo/Galileo loading status
l4_steps.output: Travelport loading confirmation report across Apollo and Galileo sub-platforms
l4_steps.kpi: Travelport schedule parity ≥99.5% within 72 hours; Apollo/Galileo consistency 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Travelport's Apollo and Galileo sub-platforms have different update cadences; inconsistency between the two creates agent booking confusion and potential duplicate or missing availability for the same flight

l4_steps.name: Monitor Amadeus GDS schedule loading across all PCCs
l4_steps.input: OAG distribution confirmation, Amadeus PCC propagation status
l4_steps.output: Amadeus parity report; consolidated GDS parity sign-off across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus
l4_steps.kpi: Amadeus schedule parity ≥99.5% within 72 hours; full PCC propagation confirmed within 96 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus GDS propagation to all Pseudo City Codes can lag by 24 hours; corporate TMC agents using affected PCCs see stale or missing schedules during the propagation window, generating avoidable calls to airline sales teams

l4_steps.name: Publish schedule to NDC API Gateway for OTA partners
l4_steps.input: Validated SSIM, approved fare inventory from Amadeus NRM
l4_steps.output: NDC offer catalog updated; API endpoint live for OTA and metasearch partners
l4_steps.kpi: NDC schedule availability within 4 hours of SSIM freeze confirmation; API offer response latency <200ms at P99
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC schema versioning (IATA NDC 21.3) mismatches with OTA partner implementations cause silent failures where offer requests return empty results with no error surfaced to the traveller; debugging requires partner-by-partner API log analysis

l4_steps.name: Update airline.com booking engine via Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Published SSIM, live fare inventory, NDC offer catalog
l4_steps.output: Live schedule displayed in airline.com booking flow with correct availability and pricing
l4_steps.kpi: Direct channel schedule accuracy 100%; booking engine page response time <3 seconds; availability parity with GDS within 1 hour of schedule publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS schedule cache refresh requires a manual trigger for urgent changes; stale cache causes customers to see phantom flights or missing flights, generating misdirected bookings and call-centre volume spikes

l4_steps.name: Execute cross-channel schedule parity audit
l4_steps.input: Published schedules from Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, NDC API, and airline.com; master SSIM as reference
l4_steps.output: Cross-channel parity audit report with discrepancy log (flight number, date, affected channel, nature of mismatch)
l4_steps.kpi: Cross-channel schedule parity ≥99.8% within 5 business days of initial load; audit covering 100% of new and changed flights
l4_steps.pain_point: No real-time automated parity monitoring tool spans all five distribution channels simultaneously; manual spot-checks via OAG miss low-frequency discrepancies such as wrong equipment type or missing return leg that only manifest at specific date ranges

l4_steps.name: Issue SSIM delta file and re-submit for channel correction
l4_steps.input: Parity audit discrepancy log with channel-specific mismatch details
l4_steps.output: SSIM delta file (update and cancel records) re-submitted to OAG; correction tracking ticket raised per affected channel
l4_steps.kpi: Critical corrections (cancellations, departure time changes >15 min) re-distributed within 4 hours; all corrections confirmed propagated within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: SSIM delta files require the same full validation cycle as the initial file; urgent corrections still take 24–48 hours to propagate across GDS batch pipelines, during which customers may purchase now-invalid itineraries requiring involuntary rerouting

l4_steps.name: Notify Revenue Management and activate NRM inventory
l4_steps.input: Final published schedule, parity audit sign-off document
l4_steps.output: NRM inventory controls activated for all new and changed flights; RM team notified with flight list and opening load factors
l4_steps.kpi: NRM inventory activation within 24 hours of schedule publication sign-off; 100% of new routes activated before booking opening date
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM inventory loading following SSIM publication is not automated; the manual handoff between Schedule Planning and Revenue Management teams introduces activation delays of 1–3 days, causing new flights to go on sale without yield controls in place and exposing the airline to underpriced early bookings

l4_steps.name: Ingest real-time disruption alerts from ops systems
l4_steps.input: Weather service alerts, ATC NOTAMs, aircraft technical fault reports
l4_steps.output: Unified disruption notification log with timestamp and source
l4_steps.kpi: Alert-to-acknowledgement time ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple alert streams (weather, ATC, maintenance) arrive in disparate systems with no unified ingestion layer, causing detection delays of 10–20 min during complex events

l4_steps.name: Classify IROPS trigger type and severity tier
l4_steps.input: Disruption notification log, affected airport and flight list
l4_steps.output: IROPS classification (weather / ATC / technical / security / crew) and severity tier (1=local, 2=regional, 3=network-wide)
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥95%; mis-classification rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: No AI-assisted triage in legacy NOC toolsets; mis-classification delays activation of the correct recovery playbook, costing 15–30 min of recovery time

l4_steps.name: Activate IROPS command structure and war room
l4_steps.input: Severity tier, affected station list, initial disruption scope
l4_steps.output: IROPS war room activated; stakeholder notifications sent to crew, commercial, ground ops, and customer relations leads
l4_steps.kpi: War room activation time ≤15 min from trigger classification
l4_steps.pain_point: Escalation contact lists frequently stale; cross-functional mobilisation relies on manual phone trees rather than automated push notifications, adding 10–20 min delay

l4_steps.name: Model affected flight propagation in network simulator
l4_steps.input: IROPS classification, affected airports, time window of disruption
l4_steps.output: Affected flight list with downstream propagation map showing knock-on cancellation risk
l4_steps.kpi: Network impact model run time ≤30 min; propagation accuracy ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM scenario setup is manual and not pre-loaded with IROPS templates; large weather events affecting 100+ flights can take 30–45 min to model, exceeding recovery window

l4_steps.name: Identify aircraft and crew positioning conflicts
l4_steps.input: Affected flight list, current crew duty records, aircraft position data
l4_steps.output: Crew duty conflict report; aircraft position conflict map with stranded-asset flags
l4_steps.kpi: Conflict identification complete ≤20 min; coverage of 100% of affected pairings
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 duty/rest legality checks are sequential in Jeppesen; large-scale events overwhelm manual review, and reserve pool visibility is not real-time

l4_steps.name: Estimate disrupted passenger volume and missed connections
l4_steps.input: Affected flight booking data from Altéa PSS, connection itinerary records
l4_steps.output: Disrupted passenger count by segment, missed connection tally, estimated rebooking inventory gap
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger impact estimate accuracy ≥85%; model run time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM is not designed for real-time IROPS queries; passenger impact models must be manually triggered outside normal RM workflow, creating data-currency risk

l4_steps.name: Assess slot and regulatory constraints at affected airports
l4_steps.input: Affected slot portfolio, airport coordination contacts, no-fly window data
l4_steps.output: Waiveable slot list, regulatory no-fly windows, ATC Ground Delay Program parameters
l4_steps.kpi: Slot waiver request accuracy ≥98%; assessment complete ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot waiver processes vary by country and airport authority; some regions require 24-hour advance notice incompatible with real-time IROPS response timelines

l4_steps.name: Generate recovery schedule scenarios in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Impact assessment outputs, available aircraft count, crew availability, slot constraints
l4_steps.output: 2–3 recovery schedule options with trade-off analysis (cost vs. OTP vs. coverage)
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario generation time ≤45 min; minimum 2 viable options produced
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS is not optimised for real-time IROPS iteration; manual schedule editing under time pressure increases the risk of SSIM errors propagating to GDS

l4_steps.name: Evaluate aircraft swap and ferry flight feasibility
l4_steps.input: Aircraft availability roster, maintenance status from AMOS, ferry routing options, positioning cost estimates
l4_steps.output: Approved ferry/swap plan or rejection rationale with cost-benefit summary
l4_steps.kpi: Ferry cost vs. delay cost ratio assessed within 30 min; SkyMAX fleet assignment feasibility score ≥0.85
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS maintenance status sync delay (up to 15 min) risks assigning aircraft with open airworthiness items; no automated maintenance-status gate in SkyMAX IROPS workflows

l4_steps.name: Validate crew legality for full recovery plan
l4_steps.input: Proposed recovery schedule, current crew duty and rest records, reserve availability
l4_steps.output: Crew-legal recovery schedule or exception list requiring reserve activation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% FAR Part 117 compliance validated before plan publication; legality check ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Iterative crew legality re-checks slow plan finalisation; each SkyWORKS schedule change triggers a full Jeppesen re-validation cycle, compounding delay when multiple iterations are needed

l4_steps.name: Publish revised recovery schedule to PSS and GDS
l4_steps.system: Amadeus SkyWORKS → Amadeus Altéa PSS → Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS
l4_steps.input: Approved, crew-legal recovery schedule
l4_steps.output: Updated schedules live in Altéa PSS, Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, and NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.kpi: GDS schedule update latency ≤30 min from approval; distribution completeness 100% of active channels
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-channel distribution (Altéa + Sabre + Travelport + NDC) requires sequential pushes with no atomic commit; partial-update windows create booking inconsistencies and duplicate inventory

l4_steps.name: File slot waivers and coordinate ATC ground delay program
l4_steps.input: Waiveable slot list, ATC GDP parameters, airport authority contacts
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot waivers, revised approved departure windows per airport
l4_steps.kpi: Slot waiver approval rate ≥90%; ATC GDP compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC GDP parameters change frequently during active weather events; real-time coordination requires a dedicated FAA/EUROCONTROL liaison channel that is not always staffed at smaller carriers

l4_steps.name: Confirm and dispatch aircraft ferry repositioning flights
l4_steps.input: Approved swap/ferry plan, ATC clearances, confirmed slot windows
l4_steps.output: Filed flight plans for ferry flights, repositioning confirmation messages to stations
l4_steps.kpi: Ferry flight OTP ≥75%; repositioning within ±2 hrs of recovery plan target
l4_steps.pain_point: Ferry flight fuel burn is not pre-budgeted in standard IROPS cost models; post-event cost attribution to IROPS events is a manual, multi-week reconciliation process

l4_steps.name: Initiate automated passenger rebooking
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Disrupted passenger list, recovery flight inventory, passenger tier (FFP status)
l4_steps.output: Rebooking confirmations sent to passengers; exception queue for manual handling
l4_steps.kpi: Automated rebooking rate ≥70%; passenger notification delivered ≤30 min of flight cancellation
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa automated rebooking rules are not always tuned for IROPS scenarios; high-volume events exhaust available recovery inventory before all passengers are rebooked, forcing costly offline handling

l4_steps.name: Activate reserve crew and complete crew reassignments
l4_steps.input: Recovery schedule, crew conflict report, reserve crew availability and location
l4_steps.output: Final crew assignments for all recovery flights; reserve activation orders issued
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve activation time ≤45 min; crew coverage rate ≥98% of recovery flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew contact and activation is phone-based at many carriers; no push-notification system for mass activation means manual calling campaigns during high-stress IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Issue passenger care and compensation entitlements
l4_steps.input: Delay/cancellation duration, disruption cause classification, passenger loyalty tier
l4_steps.output: Meal vouchers, hotel authorisations, transport allowances, and DOT/EU261 compensation notices
l4_steps.kpi: DOT / EU261 compensation filing accuracy ≥99%; voucher issuance within 60 min of entitlement trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Compensation eligibility rules differ by jurisdiction (DOT, EU261, ANAC, DGAC); no unified entitlement engine forces manual legal review for international itineraries, creating under- or over-payment risk

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-IROPS cost and performance analysis
l4_steps.input: Ferry fuel invoices, compensation payouts, rebooking costs, OTP and cancellation data
l4_steps.output: IROPS total cost report, OTP and cancellation deviation analysis vs. plan
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered ≤72 hrs post-event; cost capture accuracy ±2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cost data is scattered across Altéa (compensation), SAP (vendor invoices), and Jeppesen (crew overtime); manual reconciliation typically takes 5–7 business days, delaying learning cycle

l4_steps.name: Update IROPS recovery playbooks and SkySYM scenario library
l4_steps.input: Post-event debrief findings, scenario performance data, cost report
l4_steps.output: Updated recovery playbook version; new scenario added to SkySYM IROPS library for future use
l4_steps.kpi: Playbook updated within 30 days of event; ≥1 new SkySYM scenario created per Tier 2+ IROPS
l4_steps.pain_point: Playbook updates are routinely deprioritised once normal operations resume; institutional recovery knowledge is frequently lost without a mandatory structured capture and review process

l4_steps.name: Receive & Log Charter Request
l4_steps.input: Client inquiry or broker RFQ (route, date, pax count, special requirements)
l4_steps.output: Logged charter request with unique reference number
l4_steps.kpi: Request-to-quote turnaround ≤4 hours of receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: No standardised intake form; requests arrive via email, phone, and broker portals with inconsistent data quality, causing re-work before feasibility can begin

l4_steps.name: Validate Route & Airport Feasibility
l4_steps.input: Charter request log, airport infrastructure database, bilateral ASA register
l4_steps.output: Feasibility report covering range, runway length, curfews, and handling agent availability
l4_steps.kpi: Feasibility assessment completed ≤2 hours of request receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport infrastructure constraints (runway PCN, curfews, Category III ILS availability) not always current in SkySYM, requiring manual NOTAM and AIP cross-check

l4_steps.name: Assess Fleet Availability for Charter Date
l4_steps.input: Current published schedule, maintenance release plan, feasibility report
l4_steps.output: Available aircraft list with candidate tail numbers and estimated positioning cost
l4_steps.kpi: Charter fleet utilisation rate ≥85% on confirmed charter days
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter demand routinely conflicts with peak scheduled operations; no dedicated charter fleet buffer exists, forcing displacement of scheduled rotations

l4_steps.name: Verify Air Service Agreements & Permit Scope
l4_steps.input: Feasibility report, destination country, charter type (commercial, private, government)
l4_steps.output: List of required permits, bilateral ASA status, advance-notice windows per country
l4_steps.kpi: Permit scope identified ≤1 business day of feasibility sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: ASA gaps for new international charter destinations; some governments (Middle East, West Africa) require 72–120 hours advance notice, invalidating short-lead requests

l4_steps.name: Apply for Overflight & Landing Permits
l4_steps.input: Permit requirement list, aircraft registration, ICAO flight identifiers
l4_steps.output: Filed permit applications, confirmation numbers, expected approval timeline
l4_steps.kpi: Permit approval rate ≥95% within 48 hours of application
l4_steps.pain_point: Permit rejections or multi-day delays from foreign CAAs can invalidate charter date commitments already communicated to clients; no automated status polling in SITA system

l4_steps.name: Coordinate Airport Slot & Ground Handler
l4_steps.input: Approved permits, flight schedule details, preferred handling agent contracts
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot allocation, ground handler assignment, and fuelling agreement
l4_steps.kpi: Slot secured ≥5 days before departure; ground handler confirmed ≥72 hours before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Ad-hoc charter requests often arrive within 48 hours of departure, leaving no slot buffer at Level 3 coordinated airports; late slots attract handling surcharges of 30–50% above standard rates

l4_steps.name: Assign Aircraft Tail & Confirm MX Release
l4_steps.input: Available aircraft list, maintenance schedule, MEL status log
l4_steps.output: Confirmed tail number with maintenance release, deferred defect check complete
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft assigned ≥72 hours before departure; MX release confirmed ≥24 hours before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute MEL findings discovered during pre-departure inspection force tail swaps after crew pairing, catering, and ground handler briefings are complete, causing cascading delays

l4_steps.name: Build Crew Pairing Within FAR Part 117 Limits
l4_steps.input: Confirmed tail number, route, departure and arrival times, crew qualifications database
l4_steps.output: Charter crew pairing with duty-time compliance check, rest period validated
l4_steps.kpi: Crew assignment completed ≥48 hours before departure; 100% FAR Part 117 duty compliance
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter routes often exceed standard trip lengths or require international type ratings (ETOPS or specific country approvals); limited qualified crew pool for remote or new destinations

l4_steps.name: Confirm Special Handling & Catering Requirements
l4_steps.input: Client brief (VIP specifications, cargo manifest, special meal codes, security requirements)
l4_steps.output: Special service order confirmed with caterer, ground handler, and security provider
l4_steps.kpi: Special service confirmation delivered ≤24 hours after crew assignment
l4_steps.pain_point: VIP and government charter clients frequently request bespoke catering and in-cabin configurations incompatible with standard galley setup; last-minute changes after catering uplift incur waste costs

l4_steps.name: Calculate All-In Charter Price & Margin
l4_steps.input: Route details, current fuel price (Platts jet fuel index), airport fees, crew cost, handling cost, positioning leg cost
l4_steps.output: Itemised price quote with gross margin analysis and fuel surcharge buffer
l4_steps.kpi: Gross margin on charter ≥15% above direct operating cost; quote issued ≤2 hours of feasibility confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel price volatility between quote acceptance and flight date creates margin erosion; no automatic fuel surcharge adjustment mechanism is integrated into the charter pricing model

l4_steps.name: Issue Charter Contract & Collect Deposit
l4_steps.input: Approved price quote, client details, payment terms
l4_steps.output: Executed charter contract via DocuSign, 25% deposit posted to AR in SAP
l4_steps.kpi: Contract executed ≤24 hours of quote acceptance; deposit received ≥5 days before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Payment delays from charter brokers are common; deposit terms not enforced consistently; SAP AR integration gaps mean charter revenue recognition is sometimes deferred to the following month-end

l4_steps.name: Load Charter Flight into PSS & Block Inventory
l4_steps.input: Signed contract, final pax manifest, special service order
l4_steps.output: Active charter flight record in Altéa, inventory fully blocked, IATA SSR codes applied
l4_steps.kpi: Flight created in PSS ≤4 hours of contract execution; zero open inventory seats on charter segment
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter flights must be created as special service segments in Altéa; misclassification as scheduled flights causes revenue leakage and double-counting in RM yield reporting

l4_steps.name: File ICAO Flight Plan & Check NOTAMs
l4_steps.input: Confirmed route, tail number, fuel uplift plan, departure time
l4_steps.output: Filed ICAO flight plan, NOTAM briefing pack, alternate aerodrome selected
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan filed ≥3 hours before STD; NOTAM briefing completed ≥90 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute NOTAM closures (runway, restricted airspace, volcanic ash advisories) require re-routing; no automated re-route trigger exists for charter flights outside the scheduled network

l4_steps.name: Conduct Pre-Departure Crew & Cabin Briefing
l4_steps.input: Crew pairing, filed flight plan, weather package, special service order, security threat level
l4_steps.output: Signed crew briefing record, cabin configuration confirmed, security clearances verified
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing completed ≥90 min before STD; 100% crew attendance confirmed
l4_steps.pain_point: VIP or government charter clients sometimes request last-minute route or timing changes post-briefing, requiring flight plan amendment and potential slot forfeiture at the destination

l4_steps.name: Execute Charter Flight & Capture Actuals
l4_steps.input: Pre-departure checks complete, ATC clearance received, pax aboard
l4_steps.output: Actual block time, fuel burn, pax count, and any ATC deviation logged in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Block time variance ≤10 min vs. planned; fuel burn within ±3% of flight plan estimate
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC delays on ad-hoc routes not automatically captured in Altéa; actual fuel and time data require manual post-flight reconciliation, creating a 24–48 hour reporting lag

l4_steps.name: Reconcile Charter Revenue & Costs in SAP
l4_steps.input: Actual flight data from Altéa, supplier invoices (fuel, catering, handling, permits)
l4_steps.output: Charter P&L report, variance analysis vs. quoted price, cost centre allocation
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue recognition completed ≤5 business days of flight; invoice matching rate ≥90% automated
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter cost allocation to cost centres is manual; catering and handling invoices frequently arrive 30+ days post-flight, requiring accruals that distort period-end reporting

l4_steps.name: Update Charter Pricing Model & Lessons Learned
l4_steps.input: Charter P&L report, operational incident log, client satisfaction feedback
l4_steps.output: Updated charter pricing model parameters, lessons-learned record published in Tableau dashboard
l4_steps.kpi: Pricing model refresh cycle: quarterly; margin forecast accuracy improvement ≥5% per cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Lessons-learned data are not systematically fed back into the charter pricing model; repeat cost overruns on the same international routes indicate a structural feedback loop gap

l4_steps.name: Extract competitor schedule data from OAG feed
l4_steps.input: Weekly OAG data subscription refresh (SSIM-format schedule file)
l4_steps.output: Structured competitor schedule dataset by route, frequency, and aircraft type
