l4_steps.kpi: Data currency: schedule feed ≤7 days old; coverage ≥95% of target markets
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG schedule data lags actual GDS availability by 24–72 hrs; codeshare operating vs marketing carrier misclassification inflates competitor frequency counts

l4_steps.name: Ingest DOT Form 41 traffic and capacity statistics
l4_steps.input: US DOT BTS Form 41 quarterly release (T-100 domestic segment data)
l4_steps.output: Market-level ASM, RPM, and enplanement records loaded to Redshift
l4_steps.kpi: Ingestion completeness ≥99% of published BTS records; pipeline SLA <4 hrs post-BTS release
l4_steps.pain_point: T-100 data is released with a 60-day lag; ultra-LCC capacity additions are visible in OAG weeks before T-100 confirms actual operation

l4_steps.name: Pull GDS booking and availability data for share estimation
l4_steps.input: Sabre MarketIntelligence booking data extract; Amadeus GDS availability snapshot
l4_steps.output: Point-of-sale booking share estimates by O&D market and carrier
l4_steps.kpi: Market coverage: GDS data represents ≥70% of bookable seats on target routes
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC channel bookings bypass GDS; LCC direct-channel share is structurally underrepresented, causing systematic underestimation of competitor capture rate

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness and trigger re-pull if gaps detected
l4_steps.input: Automated data quality report from Redshift completeness checks
l4_steps.output: Data validation sign-off or re-pull request to upstream pipeline
l4_steps.kpi: Data quality gate pass rate ≥98% before advancing to analysis phase
l4_steps.pain_point: Partial OAG refreshes due to airline filing delays leave gaps for low-frequency international routes; manual gap-filling introduces analyst subjectivity

l4_steps.name: Map competitor frequency and timing by route
l4_steps.input: Validated competitor schedule dataset from Step 1.4
l4_steps.output: Frequency matrix by competitor, route, and departure time bank
l4_steps.kpi: Frequency gap identified on ≥80% of monitored routes within 5 business days of OAG refresh
l4_steps.pain_point: Ultra-LCC seasonal schedule volatility (Spirit, Frontier) makes frequency comparisons unstable; weekly snapshots miss intra-week capacity dumping tactics

l4_steps.name: Assess competitor fleet gauge and seat capacity per route
l4_steps.input: SSIM aircraft type codes from OAG feed; Amadeus SkyWORKS fleet reference table
l4_steps.output: Seat capacity report per competitor flight by route and equipment type
l4_steps.kpi: Seat capacity variance vs prior period flagged within ±5% accuracy against T-100 actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: SSIM equipment codes are often filed as generic family codes (e.g. 32A for any A320-family) making true gauge differentiation between A319/A320/A321neo unreliable

l4_steps.name: Identify competitive schedule gaps and overlap windows
l4_steps.input: Frequency matrix and seat capacity report from Steps 2.1–2.2
l4_steps.output: Route priority list ranked by competitive exposure score; whitespace opportunity map
l4_steps.kpi: ≥5 whitespace route opportunities or ≥3 overlap-reduction candidates identified per quarterly cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM scenario modelling requires manual O&D demand curves as input; stale demand assumptions from pre-COVID traffic models skew gap analysis in recovering thin markets

l4_steps.name: Determine whether material competitive threat warrants escalation
l4_steps.input: Competitive exposure score and whitespace map from Step 2.3
l4_steps.output: Decision: escalate to capacity modelling (Y) or archive for quarterly review (N)
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation decision issued within 5 business days of schedule gap analysis completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold for 'material threat' is qualitatively defined; no standardised scoring rubric causes inconsistent escalation patterns across different analyst teams

l4_steps.name: Compute ASM and RPM trends versus industry peers
l4_steps.input: T-100 records and OAG capacity data from Redshift; peer carrier selection list
l4_steps.output: Rolling 12-month ASM/RPM trend report vs peer group (e.g. Delta, United, Southwest)
l4_steps.kpi: ASM CAGR benchmarked against top-5 network carriers; report produced within 3 days of T-100 release
l4_steps.pain_point: Peer group selection is subjective; including ULCCs in the peer set distorts unit cost benchmarks given fundamentally different cost structures and ancillary revenue models

l4_steps.name: Benchmark CASK and RASK against published Form 41 data
l4_steps.input: DOT Form 41 P-12 financial schedules; internal cost allocation data from SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.output: CASK/RASK variance report with carrier ranking and gap-to-best-in-class analysis
l4_steps.kpi: RASK within ±3% of peer median; CASK gap-to-best flagged if >10% adverse variance
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP FI/CO cost data uses internal cost centre allocations that differ from DOT Form 41 reporting categories; reconciliation requires manual mapping table maintenance

l4_steps.name: Evaluate whether own metrics fall below benchmark thresholds
l4_steps.input: CASK/RASK variance report and ASM/RPM trend analysis
l4_steps.output: Benchmark status flag: within tolerance / below threshold / critical gap
l4_steps.kpi: Benchmark review cycle completed quarterly; critical gaps escalated to VP Network within 48 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Power BI dashboards pull from Redshift snapshots with a 24-hr lag; real-time competitive capacity changes triggered by fare sales are invisible until next refresh cycle

l4_steps.name: Run O&D traffic share analysis by market
l4_steps.input: GDS booking share data; T-100 O&D traffic estimates; SkyCAST demand model
l4_steps.output: Market share report by O&D pair: own share vs top-3 competitors, trend over 8 quarters
l4_steps.kpi: Market share tracking coverage ≥90% of top-50 O&D markets by revenue; report cycle ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D demand models are calibrated on historical traffic; post-pandemic leisure demand shift to off-peak O&D pairs is not yet fully reflected in SkyCAST baseline assumptions

l4_steps.name: Model revenue impact of competitor capacity changes
l4_steps.input: Market share report; competitor capacity delta from Phase 2; SkySYM demand elasticity curves
l4_steps.output: Revenue impact model: projected incremental revenue gain/loss under each competitive scenario
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue impact model completed within 5 business days; scenario accuracy validated against last 4 actuals within ±8%
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM demand elasticity parameters require periodic recalibration; outdated elasticities overestimate diversion from legacy network carriers and underestimate LCC price sensitivity

l4_steps.name: Assess whether schedule response is justified by revenue model
l4_steps.input: Revenue impact model from Step 4.2; available fleet and crew headroom data
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision on capacity response; disposition for each flagged route
l4_steps.kpi: Decision issued within 3 business days of revenue model delivery; routes with projected NPV >$500K fast-tracked to schedule change workflow
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet headroom data from the crew system and SkyMAX fleet assignment may reflect tentative aircraft swaps not yet confirmed; committing capacity response against uncommitted fleet creates downstream conflict

l4_steps.name: Draft capacity response and schedule recommendations
l4_steps.input: Approved route disposition list from Step 4.3; current season schedule in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Draft schedule change request: frequency additions, gauge upgrades, or withdrawals with effective dates
l4_steps.kpi: Draft recommendations delivered within 5 business days of go-decision; SSIM-formatted change files ready for slot filing
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS schedule change workflow requires SSIM files to comply with IATA Season A/B slot deadlines; competitive response decisions made mid-season often miss the coordinated season window

l4_steps.name: Cross-validate recommendations with Amadeus NRM inventory
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule change request; NRM current fare class inventory and booking pace
l4_steps.output: NRM alignment sign-off or revised recommendation with RM-adjusted timing/frequency
l4_steps.kpi: NRM review completed within 3 business days; <10% of recommendations require material revision due to inventory conflict
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM inventory controls are set per flight departure; schedule changes that shift flights to new time slots reset booking pace baselines and require NRM recalibration, creating a 2–3 week blind spot in yield management

l4_steps.name: Submit approved schedule changes to planning queue
l4_steps.input: NRM-approved schedule change request; IATA slot filing deadlines
l4_steps.output: Confirmed schedule change submitted to SkyWORKS production queue; IATA CRS slot filing initiated where required
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of approved changes submitted within IATA CRS filing window; zero capacity responses missed due to deadline breach
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA CRS coordinated slot filings at Level 3 airports (e.g. LHR, JFK) require bilateral coordination that can delay competitive response by 3–6 months; uncoordinated airports still subject to airlines' own scheduling freeze windows

l4_steps.name: Extract competitive schedule & capacity data
l4_steps.input: Annual planning cycle trigger; prior-year SSIM schedules
l4_steps.output: Competitor capacity matrix by O&D market (seats, frequencies, ASMs)
l4_steps.kpi: Market coverage: ≥95% of OAG universe validated within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data lags 48–72 hrs for LCC schedule changes; analyst must reconcile against GDS live availability

l4_steps.name: Ingest historical O&D traffic & yield data
l4_steps.input: 3-year rolling MIDT booking data, internal ticket coupon data
l4_steps.output: O&D demand baseline with seasonality indices per market pair
l4_steps.kpi: Demand model R² ≥0.90 vs actual bookings on back-test
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT coverage drops to ~60% for LCC-heavy markets where GDS penetration is low; distorts baseline

l4_steps.name: Validate & cleanse market intelligence dataset
l4_steps.input: OAG capacity matrix, SkyCAST O&D baseline, macroeconomic indices
l4_steps.output: Validated market intelligence dataset approved for modelling
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥98% of target O&D pairs before model run
l4_steps.pain_point: Macro data (GDP, tourism forecasts) sourced from multiple external vendors with inconsistent update cycles

l4_steps.name: Generate long-haul & medium-haul demand scenarios
l4_steps.input: Validated market intelligence dataset; strategic growth targets from CEO brief
l4_steps.output: 3 demand scenarios (base, upside, downside) per O&D market for 3-year horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario variance within ±15% of base-case for primary markets
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM scenario runtime scales poorly for networks >500 O&D pairs; overnight batch required for full network runs

l4_steps.name: Score and rank route opportunities by strategic fit
l4_steps.input: 3 demand scenarios, strategic priority filters (geography, alliance fit, connectivity)
l4_steps.output: Ranked route opportunity scorecard (revenue potential, strategic score, competitive intensity)
l4_steps.kpi: Top-20 route list updated within 2 weeks of scenario generation
l4_steps.pain_point: Scoring weights for 'strategic fit' are subjective; senior stakeholders override quantitative ranking without documented rationale

l4_steps.name: Review route shortlist against network strategy guardrails
l4_steps.input: Ranked route opportunity scorecard, board-approved network strategy KPIs
l4_steps.output: Approved route shortlist (10–30 routes) for feasibility analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Shortlist approved within 5 business days of scorecard publication
l4_steps.pain_point: No system-enforced guardrail check; planner reliance on manual KPI dashboard review risks missing constraints

l4_steps.name: Run fleet assignment optimisation for shortlisted routes
l4_steps.input: Approved route shortlist, current fleet plan, aircraft availability calendar
l4_steps.output: Fleet assignment plan with gauge recommendations per route
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet utilisation uplift ≥2% vs current plan in optimised output
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX optimisation assumes unconstrained maintenance slots; MRO visit conflicts discovered post-optimisation require manual iteration

l4_steps.name: Assess slot & airport capacity constraints
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment plan, IATA WSG slot library for target airports
l4_steps.output: Slot feasibility report (available, historic grandfather, needs application)
l4_steps.kpi: Slot feasibility assessment completed ≥90 days before IATA scheduling conference
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot availability at Level 3 airports (LHR, AMS, CDG) is opaque until conference; strategic plans regularly revised post-conference

l4_steps.name: Evaluate airport infrastructure & ground handling readiness
l4_steps.input: Slot feasibility report, proposed frequencies, aircraft gauge
l4_steps.output: Airport readiness assessment (gates, ground handlers, customs, fuelling)
l4_steps.kpi: Infrastructure gap identified ≥12 months before proposed launch date
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground handler capacity data at outstations not centrally held; planner must contact handlers individually, adding 3–6 weeks to cycle

l4_steps.name: Confirm operational feasibility of candidate routes
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment plan, slot feasibility report, airport readiness assessment
l4_steps.output: Operationally feasible route set confirmed in SkyWORKS schedule editor
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of shortlisted routes confirmed feasible without major constraint
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew base restrictions and FAR Part 117 duty-time rules reduce feasible rotations, particularly for ultra-long-haul additions

l4_steps.name: Build unit revenue & yield forecast per candidate route
l4_steps.input: Confirmed feasible route set, demand scenarios, competitive fare data from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: PRASM and RASM forecast per route across base/upside/downside scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: RASM forecast accuracy within ±8% of actuals on launched routes (tracked retrospectively)
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM is calibrated on existing routes; forecast reliability for new O&D markets with no booking history is low — often requires manual analyst override

l4_steps.name: Model direct operating costs per route
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment plan (aircraft type, block hours), fuel price assumptions, airport charges schedule
l4_steps.output: CASM breakdown per route (fuel, airport, crew, maintenance, overhead allocation)
l4_steps.kpi: CASM model completed within 10 business days of receiving fleet assignment input
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport charge schedules for new markets are not always available in SAP master data; finance team must source bilaterally from airport authorities

l4_steps.name: Assess route contribution margin and breakeven load factor
l4_steps.input: RASM forecast, CASM breakdown, targeted load factor assumptions
l4_steps.output: Route P&L summary with breakeven load factor and payback period
l4_steps.kpi: Target contribution margin ≥12% in Year 2; breakeven load factor ≤75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sensitivity of breakeven load factor to fuel price is high; +10% fuel swing shifts breakeven by 4–6 ppts, making many routes marginal

l4_steps.name: Aggregate network business case for plan period
l4_steps.input: Individual route P&L summaries, network-level synergy assumptions (feed, connectivity)
l4_steps.output: 3-year network business case document (revenue, cost, EBIT impact)
l4_steps.kpi: Network EBIT uplift ≥$150M over plan period vs do-nothing baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Network synergy benefits (connecting traffic uplift) are difficult to isolate and often overstated in bottom-up aggregation

l4_steps.name: Package strategic plan for governance review
l4_steps.input: Network business case, route scorecard, risk register
l4_steps.output: Executive briefing pack: network strategy summary, investment ask, risk matrix
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing pack issued ≥5 business days before Network Strategy Committee meeting
l4_steps.pain_point: Version control of the briefing pack is manual; late assumption changes from Revenue Management or Finance require last-minute slides rebuild

l4_steps.name: Present plan to Network Strategy Committee
l4_steps.input: Executive briefing pack, committee member pre-read questions
l4_steps.output: Committee decision: approved / approved with conditions / rejected with rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Committee decision reached in ≤2 review cycles (no more than 1 deferral per plan)
l4_steps.pain_point: Committee quorum requires C-suite attendance; scheduling conflicts routinely delay decision by 2–4 weeks, compressing scheduling window

l4_steps.name: Publish approved strategic network plan & handoff to scheduling
l4_steps.input: Approved committee decision, final route list with gauge and frequency targets
l4_steps.output: Published strategic network plan loaded into SkyWORKS as planning baseline for Schedule Planning team
l4_steps.kpi: Plan published in SkyWORKS ≤3 business days after committee approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS baseline lock-in creates downstream rigidity; late executive changes after publication require formal change request and delay tactical planning

l4_steps.name: Ingest booking & flown data from PSS
l4_steps.input: Daily booking transactions, flown coupon data, no-show records
l4_steps.output: Cleansed booking data feed loaded into RM data warehouse
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥ 99.5% of all PNRs reconciled within 2 hours of departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS coupon reconciliation latency can delay same-day close files by up to 4 hours, compressing the overnight optimisation window

l4_steps.name: Enrich data with competitive fare & schedule feeds
l4_steps.input: Competitor published schedules, OAG fare feeds, MIDT booking data
l4_steps.output: Competitive context dataset appended to demand input files
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive fare parity check completed for 100% of O&D pairs within planning horizon
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT data lags actuals by 3–5 days, reducing confidence in competitor load factor estimates for near-term departures

l4_steps.name: Run O&D demand forecast model
l4_steps.input: Cleansed booking data, competitive context, seasonal index, special-event calendar
l4_steps.output: O&D demand forecast by booking class for 330-day horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast MAPE ≤ 15% at O&D level for departures within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand models trained on pre-2020 data underweight volatile post-COVID travel patterns; requires periodic manual seasonality overrides

l4_steps.name: Validate forecast accuracy against holdout set
l4_steps.input: O&D demand forecast, 30-day actuals from previous cycle
l4_steps.output: Forecast accuracy report; approved or rejected forecast
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast MAPE ≤ 15%; rejection triggers reforecast within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Redshift query contention during peak batch windows can delay accuracy checks, pushing AU updates past the 02:00 optimisation deadline

l4_steps.name: Define booking class hierarchy and nested buckets
l4_steps.input: Approved fare class structure from Pricing team, ATPCO filed classes
l4_steps.output: Booking class hierarchy configuration in NRM (Y, B, M, H, Q, K … buckets)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ATPCO-filed fare classes mapped to NRM booking classes before schedule activation
l4_steps.pain_point: Misalignment between ATPCO fare basis codes and NRM class definitions causes availability mismatches in GDS displays, leading to revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Set authorization unit (AU) levels per fare class
l4_steps.input: O&D demand forecast, fare class hierarchy, historical sell-up curves
l4_steps.output: Initial AU limits loaded per booking class per flight
l4_steps.kpi: AU initialisation completed for 100% of flights ≥ 90 days prior to departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual AU overrides by market analysts outside NRM create version conflicts; no audit trail for override rationale increases regulatory audit risk

l4_steps.name: Validate fare class mappings against ATPCO filings
l4_steps.input: NRM booking class configuration, ATPCO fare tariff tables
l4_steps.output: Validated or flagged class mapping; exceptions escalated to Pricing team
l4_steps.kpi: Zero GDS availability mismatches attributable to class mapping errors post-activation
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing changes by competitors can trigger a same-day re-mapping requirement; NRM does not auto-ingest ATPCO tariff updates in real time

l4_steps.name: Activate nested inventory controls in Altéa
l4_steps.input: Validated AU levels from NRM
l4_steps.output: Live nested availability published to Altéa and GDS channels
l4_steps.kpi: Availability synchronisation latency Altéa → GDS ≤ 5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa availability propagation to Sabre and Travelport GDS can lag by up to 15 minutes during peak filing windows, creating booking class sell-out errors

l4_steps.name: Run EMSRb / O&D seat allocation optimisation
l4_steps.input: AU levels, demand forecast, fare values, seat capacity
l4_steps.output: Optimised AU recommendations per booking class per flight leg
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue per available seat kilometre (RASK) improvement ≥ 2% vs baseline AU
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM O&D optimiser requires full network connectivity data; partial connectivity caused by codeshare partner IT gaps degrades optimisation quality

l4_steps.name: Review and approve AU recommendations
l4_steps.input: NRM-generated AU recommendations, market performance dashboard
l4_steps.output: Approved or manually overridden AU file
l4_steps.kpi: Analyst review cycle ≤ 90 minutes per market cluster; override rate ≤ 20%
l4_steps.pain_point: High override rates in thin O&D markets indicate NRM model underfitting; manual overrides are not fed back into the model, perpetuating forecast error

l4_steps.name: Apply approved AU updates to live inventory
l4_steps.input: Approved AU file
l4_steps.output: Updated live availability across all GDS and direct channels
l4_steps.kpi: AU update applied to 100% of affected flights within 30 minutes of approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk AU update jobs during peak hours can queue behind other NRM batch processes, delaying availability changes for same-day and next-day departures

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking pace against forecast curve
l4_steps.input: Real-time booking data from Altéa, forecast pace curve
l4_steps.output: Pace deviation alert for flights outside ±10% of forecast
l4_steps.kpi: Analyst response to pace deviation alert ≤ 2 hours for departures within 14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pull from AWS Redshift snapshots with 1-hour refresh lag; real-time anomalies for high-demand events (concerts, sports) are missed until the next refresh

l4_steps.name: Apply sell-up action or open lower classes
l4_steps.input: Pace deviation alert, current AU levels, fare class sell-up elasticity data
l4_steps.output: Revised AUs triggering sell-up (close lower classes) or stimulation (open lower classes)
l4_steps.kpi: Yield improvement ≥ 1.5% per sell-up intervention vs control flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Sell-up elasticity coefficients in NRM are recalibrated only quarterly; rapid fare environment changes (fuel surcharge adjustments) make coefficients stale within weeks

l4_steps.name: Update bid prices for O&D revenue integrity
l4_steps.input: Real-time load factors, revised demand signals, network connection values
l4_steps.output: Updated bid price vector published to Altéa for itinerary acceptance control
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price refresh cycle ≤ 4 hours for flights within 7 days of departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Bid price vector updates are network-wide calculations; during irregular ops, displaced passengers and re-accommodation can invalidate bid prices across 30+ connected flights simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Manage group booking displacement impact
l4_steps.input: Group booking request (≥10 pax), current individual seat availability
l4_steps.output: Group AU block allocated or declined; displacement cost calculated
l4_steps.kpi: Group displacement cost ≤ 8% of group revenue contribution on affected flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa group allotment module does not integrate real-time NRM bid prices; group pricing decisions rely on analyst manual look-up, creating inconsistent displacement cost accounting

l4_steps.name: Capture post-departure spill and spoilage actuals
l4_steps.input: Flown manifest from Altéa, final booking class loads, denied boarding records
l4_steps.output: Spill / spoilage report by flight and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: Spill (denied boardings) ≤ 1.5% of passengers carried; spoilage (empty seats in high class) ≤ 3% of capacity
l4_steps.pain_point: Denied boarding data from airport check-in is not always tagged with the booking class of the displaced passenger, reducing spill attribution accuracy

l4_steps.name: Evaluate forecast model performance and recalibrate
l4_steps.input: Spill / spoilage report, forecast vs actual load factor comparison
l4_steps.output: Updated SkyCAST model parameters; recalibration report
l4_steps.kpi: Model recalibration completed within 5 business days of departure; MAPE improvement ≥ 1 pp per calibration cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST model recalibration requires manual parameter uploads; there is no automated feedback loop from NRM actuals to SkyCAST, creating a 5–7 day lag in model learning

l4_steps.name: Publish yield performance report to stakeholders
l4_steps.input: RASK actuals, load factor, yield, spill/spoilage KPIs from Redshift
l4_steps.output: Weekly yield performance report distributed to VP Revenue Management and Network Planning
l4_steps.kpi: Report published within 2 business days of week close; RASK vs budget variance explained for all markets > ±3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data assembly from Altéa, NRM, and Redshift for the weekly report takes 6–8 analyst hours; no single integrated reporting layer across PSS and RM systems

l4_steps.name: Define fare class hierarchy in PSS
l4_steps.input: Fare product strategy brief, IATA booking class standards
l4_steps.output: Booking class configuration (Y, B, M, H, K, Q, V, W, L, G) in PSS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active fare products mapped to a booking class within 2 business days of product launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa booking class table has finite slots; adding new classes for ancillary bundles requires PSS configuration freeze that blocks concurrent distribution updates

l4_steps.name: Map booking classes to RM fare buckets
l4_steps.input: Booking class list from Altéa, revenue segmentation guidelines
l4_steps.output: Fare bucket mapping table in NRM linking each booking class to O&D revenue tier
l4_steps.kpi: Zero mismatches between Altéa booking class codes and NRM bucket definitions at go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM fare bucket schema uses internal numeric IDs that do not auto-sync with Altéa booking class labels; manual reconciliation required after each PSS config change

l4_steps.name: Validate fare class structure against ATPCO rules
l4_steps.input: NRM bucket mapping, published ATPCO fare records (Records 1, 2, 3)
l4_steps.output: Validation report confirming booking class eligibility rules match ATPCO Cat 25 combinability and Cat 5 advance purchase restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: 0 ATPCO rule violations flagged by GDS edits at filing; audit pass rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 25 combinability rules interact with NRM bucket nesting in non-obvious ways; misalignment causes ghost inventory — classes show available in GDS but are blocked in NRM

l4_steps.name: Publish fare class availability to GDS channels
l4_steps.input: Validated booking class configuration, SSIM schedule file
l4_steps.output: Live availability display in Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS for all market O&Ds
l4_steps.kpi: GDS availability refresh latency ≤ 90 seconds from NRM availability change; GDS parity rate ≥ 99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre GDS availability cache TTL (up to 90 s) creates window where high-demand bucket closures are not yet reflected, enabling over-sell of discount classes during flash sales

l4_steps.name: Extract historical O&D booking data by fare class
l4_steps.input: Altéa booking history (24 months), departure date range for planning horizon
l4_steps.output: O&D booking curve dataset segmented by fare class, day-of-week, and booking lead time
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction covering ≥ 95% of historical departures within planning window; query SLA ≤ 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-COVID booking patterns (2021–2022) distort historical curves; including them without seasonality dampening causes demand models to under-forecast leisure peak

l4_steps.name: Run demand forecast model per O&D bucket
l4_steps.input: Historical booking curves, competitive fare inputs from OAG Schedule Analyser
l4_steps.output: Forecast demand curve per fare bucket per O&D, including unconstrained demand estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast MASE (Mean Absolute Scaled Error) ≤ 0.25 for 90-day horizon; unconstrained demand estimate within ±12% of actuals at departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM's detruncation algorithm underestimates unconstrained demand on routes with chronic sell-outs; results in systematic under-forecasting for high-yield buckets

l4_steps.name: Review forecast variance and approve bucket plan
l4_steps.input: NRM forecast output, analyst commentary on anomalous markets
l4_steps.output: Approved demand forecast for bucket sizing; markets flagged for manual review escalated
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast review cycle ≤ 48 hours before system-generated availability updates are applied; < 5% of markets requiring manual correction
l4_steps.pain_point: High analyst workload during peak schedule planning cycles forces rubber-stamping of model outputs; errors not caught until post-departure revenue review

l4_steps.name: Set initial bucket inventory levels for departure
l4_steps.input: Approved demand forecast, aircraft capacity from Amadeus SkyMAX fleet assignment
l4_steps.output: Initial bucket protection levels and booking limits per fare class per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Bucket initialisation completed ≥ 330 days before departure for all long-haul markets; ≥ 90 days for short-haul
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX fleet assignment changes propagate to NRM with up to 6-hour lag; bucket limits set against wrong aircraft type cause premature close-out of discount classes

l4_steps.name: Configure EMSR-b bid price and nesting strategy
l4_steps.input: Approved bucket protection levels, fare class revenue values, willingness-to-pay estimates
l4_steps.output: Bid price thresholds and virtual bucket nesting hierarchy loaded into NRM for each O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price calibration complete ≥ 180 days before departure for long-haul; revenue uplift from nesting vs. partitioned control ≥ 2% RASM on calibrated markets
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM's EMSR-b calculation does not natively account for ancillary revenue (bag fees, seat upgrades) in WTP estimates; bid prices structurally undervalue leisure segments

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking pace against expected S-curve
l4_steps.input: Real-time bookings from Altéa, expected booking curve from NRM forecast
l4_steps.output: Booking pace index (BPI) per flight per fare class; pace alerts for flights deviating > 20%
l4_steps.kpi: BPI monitored at T−90, T−60, T−30, T−14, T−7, T−3 checkpoints; alert resolution SLA ≤ 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM booking pace alerts have a minimum 15-minute polling interval; during flash sales or news events, early-warning signals arrive too late to prevent discount class oversell

l4_steps.name: Adjust bucket thresholds based on pace deviation
l4_steps.input: Booking pace alert, current bucket availability, revised demand estimate
l4_steps.output: Updated protection levels and booking limits; change log entry in NRM audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Bucket adjustment applied within 2 hours of pace alert; average revenue recovery per adjustment ≥ $8/seat on affected flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent intraday bucket adjustments on the same flight trigger NRM re-optimisation queue delays; changes queue behind batch jobs and may not take effect for up to 30 minutes

l4_steps.name: Open or close fare classes per booking curve triggers
l4_steps.input: NRM availability recommendation, time-to-departure trigger rules
l4_steps.output: Updated fare class availability in Altéa and reflected across GDS/NDC channels
l4_steps.kpi: Availability update propagated to all GDS endpoints within 90 seconds; close-out of discount classes ≥ T−3 on flights with load factor forecast ≥ 90%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway availability sync with Altéa runs on a separate thread from GDS availability; NDC channel may display open discount inventory up to 3 minutes after GDS close-out

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time bookings and cancellations by class
l4_steps.input: Live Altéa booking stream, cancellation and refund events
l4_steps.output: Real-time seat availability dashboard; auto-triggered re-open events when cancellations create sell-up opportunity
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue recovery from cancellation-triggered re-opens ≥ $15/seat; dashboard refresh ≤ 5-minute lag vs. Altéa booking engine
l4_steps.pain_point: High-volume cancellation events (weather, IROPS) flood NRM with availability change events; system enters degraded mode and availability updates queue, causing stale GDS displays

l4_steps.name: Process group booking requests against bucket availability
l4_steps.input: Group booking request (≥10 pax), current bucket availability, group fare contract
l4_steps.output: Group PNR with blocked inventory or counter-offer at higher fare class
l4_steps.kpi: Group booking response time ≤ 24 hours; group revenue contribution ≥ 8% of total flight revenue on managed markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa group booking module holds seats as option status for up to 72 hours; large group holds on high-demand flights suppress availability for individual high-yield bookings, eroding RASM

l4_steps.name: Review exception queue for manual intervention flights
l4_steps.input: NRM exception queue (special events, comp schedule changes, distressed inventory flags)
l4_steps.output: Prioritised list of flights requiring analyst action; override justification form initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Exception queue reviewed twice daily (09:00 and 14:00 local); < 3% of managed flights in exception state at any time
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM exception queue intermingles flights flagged by automated rules with analyst-generated annotations; high-priority items can be buried under system noise during IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Apply manual bucket override with audit justification
l4_steps.input: Approved override justification, competitor fare filing from OAG Schedule Analyser, event calendar
l4_steps.output: Manual availability override applied; audit log entry with approver, rationale, and expected revenue impact
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of manual overrides documented in NRM audit trail; post-event review shows manual overrides outperform model recommendation in ≥ 60% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM audit trail does not capture the external data (event calendars, competitor filings) that justified the override; institutional knowledge lost when analysts turn over

l4_steps.name: Generate post-departure revenue performance report
l4_steps.input: Altéa final booking close-out file, NRM forecast at departure, actual revenue by fare class
l4_steps.output: Post-departure report: RASM, load factor, yield, and spill/spoilage by bucket for each departed flight
l4_steps.kpi: Report generated within 48 hours of departure; RASM variance between actual and pre-departure NRM estimate reported for 100% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa close-out files arrive in S3 in variable formats depending on PSS version; ETL pipeline requires manual intervention approximately 3% of the time due to schema drift

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate NRM forecast model parameters
l4_steps.input: Post-departure performance reports (rolling 13 weeks), MASE trend, spill and spoilage analysis
l4_steps.output: Updated NRM model parameters; recalibration change log; improvement targets set for next review cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Quarterly recalibration reduces MASE by ≥ 0.02 vs. prior quarter; spill rate ≤ 3% and spoilage rate ≤ 5% on managed O&Ds post-calibration
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM model recalibration requires a 72-hour training window during which live availability recommendations revert to static rules; scheduling this window without impacting peak sale periods is operationally difficult

l4_steps.name: Extract booking & no-show history from PSS
l4_steps.input: Departed flight records, booking logs, check-in data — rolling 24 months
l4_steps.output: Raw no-show and cancellation dataset by flight, fare class, and booking channel
l4_steps.kpi: Dataset completeness ≥99% of departed flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS history exports require manual scheduling; ad-hoc pulls risk data truncation beyond 13-month rolling window

l4_steps.name: Segment data by route, DOW, fare class, season
l4_steps.input: Raw no-show dataset from Altéa PSS export
l4_steps.output: Segmented no-show rate matrix with confidence intervals per cluster
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum 90 observed flights per segment for statistical significance
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin markets (<5 flights/week) produce unreliable segment-level no-show rates; pooled estimates inflate overbooking risk

l4_steps.name: Run no-show forecast model and validate accuracy
l4_steps.input: Segmented no-show matrix, demand forecasts from AltéaRM
l4_steps.output: No-show show-up curve per flight cluster; model accuracy report
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast vs. actual no-show rate MAPE ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM show-up model requires retraining after major schedule restructures; post-COVID demand patterns invalidated legacy curves for 18+ months

l4_steps.name: Calibrate show-up curve by fare class and lead time
l4_steps.input: Validated no-show forecast model; approved show-up curves
l4_steps.output: Calibrated show-up probability curves published to AltéaRM overbooking module
l4_steps.kpi: Show-up curve refresh cycle ≤30 days for high-frequency routes; ≤90 days for seasonal routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare class proliferation (Basic Economy vs. flexible fares) requires separate show-up curves; legacy model treats all economy as one class

l4_steps.name: Generate recommended OB factors by flight segment
l4_steps.input: Calibrated show-up curves; target load factor ≥83%; denied boarding cost assumptions
l4_steps.output: Recommended overbooking factor per flight segment with expected IDB rate
l4_steps.kpi: Expected IDB rate ≤0.05 per 10,000 enplaned passengers (DOT Part 250 benchmark)
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM OB optimiser does not natively model denied boarding compensation cost per DOT 14 CFR 250 tiers; analyst must manually adjust factors to avoid regulatory overshoot

l4_steps.name: Apply DOT 14 CFR 250 regulatory cap and fare rule check
l4_steps.input: Recommended OB factors; ATPCO fare conditions (refundability, cancellation fees)
l4_steps.output: Compliance-reviewed OB factor set; flag for non-refundable fare interactions
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of OB factors within DOT involuntary bump compensation trigger thresholds
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-refundable Basic Economy fares have near-zero pre-departure cancellations, artificially inflating apparent show-up rates; ATPCO Rule 35 interactions must be hand-checked

l4_steps.name: Approve and publish booking limits to PSS inventory
l4_steps.input: Compliance-reviewed OB factor set; Director sign-off
l4_steps.output: Authorised overbooking limits loaded into Altéa inventory control per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Limit publication latency ≤4 hours ahead of booking horizon open; 100% of flights have an active OB limit
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa inventory control updates via batch file load — real-time limit changes mid-booking horizon require manual override in Altéa Inventory module, increasing error risk

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking pace vs. authorised OB limits
l4_steps.input: Live booking feed from Altéa PSS; authorised OB limits
l4_steps.output: Booking pace dashboard with oversale risk flags per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Alert response time ≤15 minutes of threshold breach detection
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM booking pace alerts are polled every 30 minutes; fast-filling charter diversions or flash sales can exceed limits before alerts trigger

l4_steps.name: Detect and triage oversale threshold breach
l4_steps.input: Booking pace alert; current bookings vs. authorised limit
l4_steps.output: Oversale risk classification (low / medium / high) with recommended action
l4_steps.kpi: False positive rate ≤10% of alerts triaged as high-risk
l4_steps.pain_point: Group booking blocks held in Altéa GRP segment are excluded from NRM oversale count until confirmed, masking true capacity exposure up to T-72h

l4_steps.name: Adjust OB level or close booking class dynamically
l4_steps.input: Oversale risk classification; updated show-up probability at current booking depth
l4_steps.output: Revised OB factor or booking class closure instruction applied to Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: OB adjustment applied within 30 minutes of triage decision; no flight departs with OB factor >20% above baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Closing discount booking classes to reduce oversale pressure destroys revenue on price-sensitive leisure itineraries; analyst must balance IDB risk vs. yield impact

l4_steps.name: Escalate high-risk oversale flights to RM Supervisor
l4_steps.input: High-risk oversale flag; passenger manifest; connecting itinerary exposure
l4_steps.output: Escalation note with recommended corrective action; decision to hold or reduce OB
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation-to-decision cycle time ≤1 hour; 100% of high-risk flights reviewed by T-24h
l4_steps.pain_point: Connecting passengers on interline itineraries (not native Altéa bookings) are not surfaced in NRM oversale count; last-minute IDB on these passengers triggers DOT reporting obligation

l4_steps.name: Identify oversold flights at check-in closure
l4_steps.input: Final check-in count; boarded passenger list; aircraft capacity
l4_steps.output: Confirmed oversale count and list of checked-in passengers eligible for VDB/IDB
l4_steps.kpi: Oversold flight identification completed ≥30 minutes before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS and Altéa DCS (Departure Control System) seat count reconciliation can diverge by 1-2 seats when upgrade or UMNR seat blocks are reassigned at gate

l4_steps.name: Solicit and screen volunteers for VDB compensation
l4_steps.input: Oversold count; gate board call; compensation parameters from RM Supervisor
l4_steps.output: Confirmed volunteer list with accepted compensation; rebooked itineraries in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: VDB rate ≥80% of oversale situations resolved without IDB; average VDB compensation cost ≤$350
l4_steps.pain_point: Compensation authority is set centrally by RM; gate agents cannot negotiate above the pre-approved cap without supervisor override, slowing volunteer acquisition on high-demand flights

l4_steps.name: Process involuntary denied boarding per 14 CFR 250
l4_steps.input: Confirmed oversale after VDB exhaustion; passenger priority matrix (status, fare, check-in time)
l4_steps.output: IDB passenger list; denied boarding compensation (cash/voucher at DOT-mandated 400% of OW fare, max $1,550)
l4_steps.kpi: IDB processing completed ≥15 minutes before door close; 0 IDB passengers with connecting flights missed due to rebooking delay
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT priority boarding rules (status, early check-in) conflict with RM desire to protect high-yield last-minute fares; applying the correct matrix under gate pressure is error-prone

l4_steps.name: Issue compensation and confirm rebooking for IDB/VDB pax
l4_steps.input: IDB/VDB passenger list; approved compensation values; next available flight inventory
l4_steps.output: Compensation vouchers/cash issued; confirmed rebooking on next available service; IDB event logged
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of IDB passengers offered confirmed rebooking within 2 hours; compensation issued at gate before passenger departs
l4_steps.pain_point: Electronic voucher issuance via Altéa is not integrated with the passenger's Rapid Rewards account; compensation is issued as a separate code, creating friction and loyalty defection risk

l4_steps.name: Compile post-flight IDB/VDB statistics and cost data
l4_steps.input: Altéa IDB/VDB event logs; gate agent reports; compensation cost records
l4_steps.output: IDB/VDB summary report: count, cost, route, fare class, DOW breakdown
l4_steps.kpi: Report generated within 48 hours of flight departure; 100% event capture rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate agent IDB logs in Altéa DCS are free-text fields; structured data extraction requires ETL cleanup before Redshift load, delaying post-flight analytics by up to 5 days

l4_steps.name: Review denied boarding KPIs against policy thresholds
l4_steps.input: IDB/VDB summary report; rolling 12-month trend; DOT Part 250 benchmark (0.05 IDB per 10k pax)
l4_steps.output: KPI review decision: policy adequate or recalibration required
l4_steps.kpi: IDB rate ≤0.05 per 10,000 enplaned passengers; VDB cost ≤$350 average per event
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal spikes (holiday periods, irregular operations) mask underlying OB model drift; point-in-time KPI review may miss structural deterioration in show-up accuracy

l4_steps.name: Submit DOT quarterly denied boarding compliance report
l4_steps.system: DOT Air Travel Consumer Report Submission Portal
l4_steps.input: Validated IDB/VDB statistics; carrier passenger enplanement totals
l4_steps.output: Filed DOT Part 250 quarterly report; internal compliance archive record
l4_steps.kpi: 100% on-time filing by DOT deadline (30 days after quarter end); zero restatements
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT requires IDB figures disaggregated by aircraft size categories; Altéa fleet-type tagging must be manually reconciled against FAA registration data to ensure accurate segment classification

l4_steps.name: Extract historical booking & ticketing data
l4_steps.input: Scheduled forecast cycle trigger (daily/weekly batch)
l4_steps.output: Raw booking history file by O&D, cabin, fare class and departure date
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥ 99% of expected PNR records
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS booking history exports can lag 4–6 hours in peak windows, misaligning the daily forecast cycle and causing stale AU recommendations to persist in NRM overnight

l4_steps.name: Ingest external demand & traffic signals
l4_steps.input: OAG forward schedule feed, MIDT booking data, tourism board indices
l4_steps.output: Enriched demand signal dataset merged with internal booking history
l4_steps.kpi: External signal ingestion latency ≤ 2 hours from OAG publish
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT data covers only GDS-booked itineraries, creating blind spots for NDC and direct-channel bookings — up to 30% of volume on some LCCs — leading to systematic under-forecasting on digitally distributed routes

l4_steps.name: Validate & cleanse data for anomalies
l4_steps.input: Raw booking history + external signals from steps 1.1–1.2
l4_steps.output: Cleansed, deduplicated demand dataset with anomaly flags
l4_steps.kpi: Data quality score ≥ 95%; outlier rows flagged < 2% of total
l4_steps.pain_point: COVID-era booking collapse and recovery create structural breaks in training data; models trained on pre-2020 history without explicit break-point adjustment produce load-factor forecasts biased 6–12 pts below actuals on leisure routes

l4_steps.name: Segment data by O&D, cabin and booking curve
l4_steps.input: Cleansed demand dataset
l4_steps.output: Demand time-series per O&D × cabin × day-of-week × season band
l4_steps.kpi: Segment granularity covers ≥ 95% of revenue-bearing O&D pairs
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin O&D markets (< 200 observations per departure) produce statistically unstable booking curves; SkyCAST defaults to network-level priors which can over-smooth volatile new-route ramp-ups

l4_steps.name: Identify constrained booking observations
l4_steps.input: Segmented demand series + historical AU and sell limit records
l4_steps.output: Flagged constrained observations (departures where AU was binding at close)
l4_steps.kpi: Constrained-observation detection rate ≥ 90% vs manual audit sample
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM does not retain intra-day AU change history at sufficient granularity; when AUs were changed multiple times within a day, the system only logs end-of-day state, causing the unconstraining algorithm to miss intermediate constraints

l4_steps.name: Apply EM unconstraining to constrained series
l4_steps.input: Constrained observation flags + observed booking counts
l4_steps.output: Unconstrained demand estimate per O&D × fare class × departure date
l4_steps.kpi: Unconstraining variance (CV) ≤ 5% on routes with ≥ 90% load factor
l4_steps.pain_point: Expectation-Maximisation unconstraining can diverge on very high-load routes (LF > 95%) where almost every observation is constrained — NRM falls back to simple censored-mean imputation which understates true demand by 8–15%

l4_steps.name: Validate unconstrained demand estimates
l4_steps.input: Unconstrained demand series from step 2.2
l4_steps.output: Validated unconstrained demand series approved for model input
l4_steps.kpi: Unconstrained mean ≤ 1.5× constrained mean on non-peak markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Overly aggressive unconstraining inflates unconstrained demand estimates, causing the optimiser to open excess inventory and erode yield on near-full flights — requires manual override on seasonal peak routes

l4_steps.name: Select forecasting model type per market
l4_steps.input: Validated unconstrained demand series, market volatility scores
l4_steps.output: Model configuration file: additive vs multiplicative per O&D × cabin
l4_steps.kpi: Model selection logic applied to 100% of active O&D pairs within 1 hour of data readiness
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST model selection heuristics default to additive models for thin markets regardless of demand variability; high-leisure volatile routes on short-haul thin sectors are systematically misconfigured, requiring manual analyst overrides each cycle

l4_steps.name: Apply special-event & seasonality overlays
l4_steps.input: Model config + airline event calendar (holidays, conventions, sports, disruptions)
l4_steps.output: Seasonality-adjusted demand series with event uplift / suppression factors
l4_steps.kpi: Special-event adjustment coverage: ≥ 85% of Top-100 events per quarter captured before forecast run
l4_steps.pain_point: Event calendar maintenance is manual and decentralised — network RM team and regional market managers each maintain separate lists, causing duplicate or conflicting adjustments when the same event spans multiple O&D pairs

l4_steps.name: Run O&D demand forecast in SkyCAST
l4_steps.input: Seasonality-adjusted unconstrained demand series + model config
l4_steps.output: Point and probabilistic demand forecasts per O&D × cabin × booking horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast MAPE ≤ 12% across all O&D pairs; P90 forecast coverage ≥ 80% of actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST batch forecast runs for a large network (500+ daily departures) can exceed the available processing window on peak planning days, causing downstream NRM optimisation to run on partially stale forecasts

l4_steps.name: Disaggregate O&D forecast to fare-class level
l4_steps.input: O&D demand forecasts from step 3.3 + fare class demand share curves
l4_steps.output: Fare-class level demand forecast input for EMSRb optimisation
l4_steps.kpi: Fare-class forecast disaggregation completed within 30 min of O&D forecast publish
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare-class demand share curves are estimated from historical booking curves; when airlines reprice aggressively (e.g. adding or retiring fare classes mid-season), the share curves become stale and misdirect inventory allocation toward retired buckets

l4_steps.name: Analyst review of system-generated forecasts
l4_steps.input: Fare-class demand forecasts from step 3.4, booking pace actuals
l4_steps.output: Reviewed forecast report with analyst annotations and override candidates
l4_steps.kpi: Analyst review completed within 4 hours of forecast publication; < 15% of O&D pairs require manual override
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM forecast review UI surfaces only summary metrics per market; analysts cannot drill to individual booking-curve segments without exporting to Excel, slowing root-cause investigation and increasing override latency

l4_steps.name: Apply market-level manual forecast adjustments
l4_steps.input: Override candidate list from step 4.1, competitive intelligence, sales intelligence
l4_steps.output: Adjusted demand forecast with analyst override log
l4_steps.kpi: Override accuracy (post-departure MAPE for overridden markets) ≤ 10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual overrides are not systematically back-tested; analysts who override frequently cannot tell whether their interventions improve or degrade forecast accuracy versus the unmodified system forecast, making governance of override behaviour impossible

l4_steps.name: Publish approved demand forecast to NRM
l4_steps.input: Approved fare-class demand forecast (system + analyst overrides)
l4_steps.output: Active demand forecast loaded into NRM for EMSRb optimisation cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast publish latency ≤ 30 min from analyst sign-off; 100% of departures within 330-day booking window covered
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM forecast publish is a full-replace operation — partial updates are not supported; if a publish job fails mid-run (e.g. network timeout), the system may hold a mix of new and prior-cycle forecasts, causing inconsistent AU recommendations until the next full cycle

l4_steps.name: Track post-departure forecast accuracy
l4_steps.input: Departed flight actuals (load factor, revenue, fare-class mix) vs forecast
l4_steps.output: Forecast accuracy scorecard: MAPE, bias, coverage by O&D, cabin, horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Rolling 30-day network MAPE ≤ 12%; bias (mean signed error) within ±2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-departure actuals are available only after PSS ticket coupon reconciliation (typically T+2 days), creating a 48-hour blind spot between departure and accuracy reporting that delays identification of systematic forecast failures on new routes

l4_steps.name: Detect systematic bias or model drift
l4_steps.input: Forecast accuracy scorecard from step 5.1
l4_steps.output: Bias / drift diagnostic report with affected O&D segments identified
l4_steps.kpi: Bias alert triggered when mean signed error exceeds ±3% for ≥ 5 consecutive departures on same O&D
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards for RM forecast tracking are maintained by a separate analytics team; model drift alerts depend on manual dashboard reviews rather than automated statistical process control, meaning bias can persist for 2–3 weeks before analyst intervention

l4_steps.name: Trigger model recalibration & parameter update
l4_steps.input: Bias / drift diagnostic report + recalibration threshold breach flags
l4_steps.output: Updated model coefficients and booking-curve parameters deployed to SkyCAST
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration cycle completed within 48 hours of bias-alert trigger; post-recalibration MAPE improvement ≥ 2 percentage points
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST model parameter updates require a full re-training run on the rolling 2-year history window; on large networks this can take 6–8 hours, blocking the daily forecast cycle if recalibration is triggered mid-day rather than during the overnight batch window

l4_steps.name: Receive Group Booking Request
l4_steps.input: Group booking request via SWABIZ portal, GDS, travel agency, or direct sales channel
l4_steps.output: Logged group enquiry record with O&D, travel dates, pax count, and contact details
l4_steps.kpi: Request acknowledgement within 4 business hours; ≥95% SLA compliance
l4_steps.pain_point: Requests arriving via multiple channels (email, GDS PNR, SWABIZ) require manual consolidation into Altéa — no single intake API across all channels

l4_steps.name: Validate Group Size Eligibility
l4_steps.input: Passenger count stated in group request
l4_steps.output: Eligibility determination: group (≥10 pax) or retail redirection
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of sub-threshold requests correctly redirected to retail within 1 business hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Groups splitting into sub-10 clusters to access retail fares while exploiting group seat release policies — requires cross-PNR duplicate-name detection

l4_steps.name: Check Blackout & Peak Period Restrictions
l4_steps.input: Travel date range from group request; current peak calendar in NRM
l4_steps.output: Date eligibility flag; alternate date suggestions if blocked
l4_steps.kpi: Blackout date check completed in <10 minutes; alternate date acceptance rate ≥40%
l4_steps.pain_point: Peak calendars maintained manually in NRM and not automatically synced with marketing/events calendar — agents may quote blocked dates before checking

l4_steps.name: Confirm O&D, Routing & Itinerary
l4_steps.input: Validated group request with confirmed dates and pax count
l4_steps.output: Structured group itinerary record with flight segments and class of service
l4_steps.kpi: Itinerary confirmed and filed in PSS within 2 hours of initial request
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-segment itineraries require manual linking of PNRs across codeshare or interline partners — slow process for international group bookings

l4_steps.name: Query Real-Time O&D Inventory Availability
l4_steps.input: Group itinerary with specific flight segments, dates, and fare class requirement
l4_steps.output: Current availability by booking class for each segment; load factor snapshot
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory query response in <30 seconds; data freshness lag ≤5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM availability data can lag real-time PSS inventory by up to 5 minutes during high-volume periods — group blocks booked on stale data risk overbooking

l4_steps.name: Run Displacement Cost Analysis
l4_steps.input: Requested seat block size; current booking curve; O&D demand forecast from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Displacement cost per seat (value of individual bookings that would be displaced); net revenue impact estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Displacement model accuracy ≥88% vs. actual realised revenue; analysis completed in <15 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Displacement models rely on NRM booking curves that may not fully account for last-minute premium fare uplift potential — groups in high-demand markets routinely under-priced

l4_steps.name: Assess Net Revenue Impact of Group Block
l4_steps.input: Displacement cost analysis; proposed group fare; seat block size
l4_steps.output: Net revenue positive/negative determination; RM recommendation (accept / reject / counter-date)
l4_steps.kpi: Group acceptance rate ≥65% of qualified requests; average group yield ≥85% of displacement cost
l4_steps.pain_point: Sales teams operate under volume targets that incentivise accepting revenue-negative groups — tension between group sales quota and RM yield discipline

l4_steps.name: Calculate Block Fare Using Group Pricing Model
l4_steps.input: Net revenue impact assessment; group discount policy matrix; fare class availability
l4_steps.output: Proposed group fare per pax; total block revenue estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Group fare ≥95% of minimum acceptable yield threshold; pricing turnaround ≤30 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Group pricing model does not natively integrate with ATPCO filed fares — group quotes are manual overrides that must be cross-checked against published fare rules to avoid BSP/ARC audit exceptions

l4_steps.name: Validate Fare Against Discount Authority Matrix
l4_steps.input: Proposed group fare; discount authority thresholds by market tier and season
l4_steps.output: Authority level determination: standard approval, RM manager review, or director escalation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of quotes validated against authority matrix before issue; zero out-of-authority quotes issued
l4_steps.pain_point: Discount authority matrices are updated quarterly in spreadsheets and manually imported into NRM — stale thresholds lead to incorrect authority-level routing

l4_steps.name: Generate Formal Group Quote Document
l4_steps.input: Approved group fare; name release schedule; deposit terms; ticketing deadline
l4_steps.output: Formal group quote with fare, seat block, deposit amount, name release dates, and ticketing deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Quote issued within 24 hours of request receipt; quote acceptance rate ≥55%
l4_steps.pain_point: Quote templates are maintained outside PSS in Word/PDF — manual population risks errors in fare amounts, deadlines, and contract terms; no audit trail within the booking system

l4_steps.name: Conduct Sales Negotiation with Group Organiser
l4_steps.input: Formal group quote; organiser counter-proposal (if any); competitive market rates
l4_steps.output: Agreed terms or revised counter-offer; negotiation log entry
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle ≤3 rounds to final agreement; average concession depth ≤5% below initial quote
l4_steps.pain_point: Sales managers lack real-time competitive fare visibility during negotiation — competitors' group rates not available in PRISM, forcing reliance on OAG or manual fare searches

l4_steps.name: Obtain Final RM Approval for Confirmed Terms
l4_steps.input: Final agreed group terms; revenue impact recalculation at agreed fare
l4_steps.output: RM approval stamp; booking authority granted to sales team
l4_steps.kpi: Approval response within 4 business hours; ≤10% of groups requiring director-level escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflow is email-based with no system-enforced audit trail — SOX compliance reviews frequently flag missing RM sign-offs on large group bookings

l4_steps.name: Confirm Group Booking & Collect Deposit
l4_steps.input: RM approval; signed group contract; deposit payment from organiser
l4_steps.output: Confirmed group PNR with seat block held; deposit receipt; booking confirmation to organiser
l4_steps.kpi: Deposit collection rate ≥98% of confirmed bookings; booking confirmation issued within 2 hours of receipt of signed contract
l4_steps.pain_point: Deposit processing via bank transfer requires manual reconciliation against PNR in SAP S/4HANA Finance — 2-3 day lag between payment receipt and booking confirmation causes organiser escalations

l4_steps.name: Create Seat Block in PSS Inventory
l4_steps.input: Confirmed group PNR; approved seat block size; fare class assignment
l4_steps.output: Hard-blocked seat inventory removed from open sale; group booking class activated
l4_steps.kpi: Seat block created within 1 hour of booking confirmation; zero inventory discrepancy vs. PNR
l4_steps.pain_point: Hard blocks in Altéa reduce sellable capacity visible to GDS channels immediately — premature blocking of large groups in advance of name submission increases unsold seat risk

l4_steps.name: Monitor Name Release & Ticketing Deadlines
l4_steps.input: Name release schedule from group contract; automated deadline alerts from PSS
l4_steps.output: Name submission status updates; reminder communications to group organiser
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of names submitted by first release deadline; ticketing deadline breach rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS deadline alerts are not integrated with CRM or email workflows — coordinators manually track deadlines in spreadsheets, leading to missed release dates and last-minute seat block management failures

l4_steps.name: Release Unsold Seats to Open Inventory
l4_steps.input: Final name count at ticketing deadline; remaining unoccupied seats in block
l4_steps.output: Released seats returned to NRM availability; booking class reopened for retail sale
l4_steps.kpi: Unsold seats released ≥72 hours before departure; recaptured revenue from released seats ≥60% of displacement cost on released units
l4_steps.pain_point: Late seat release (within 72 hours of departure) significantly reduces recapture probability — NRM booking curves flatten below T-3 days, leaving released group seats unsold and generating direct revenue loss

l4_steps.name: Process Final Passenger Manifest & Settlement
l4_steps.input: Final confirmed passenger names; actual tickets issued; deposit and balance payment records
l4_steps.output: Closed group PNR; final invoice; payment settled in SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.kpi: Final settlement completed within 5 business days post-travel; payment reconciliation accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Name changes and no-shows on group bookings trigger penalty fee calculations that must be manually computed and re-invoiced — no automated penalty engine in Altéa for group contracts

l4_steps.name: Calculate Revenue Variance vs. Forecast
l4_steps.input: Actual group revenue from SAP FI; forecast revenue from NRM displacement model; seat block utilisation data
l4_steps.output: Revenue variance report; yield performance vs. plan; group booking contribution analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast vs. actual variance ≤8%; group contribution to total flight revenue ≥12% on applicable routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue data from SAP FI and NRM actuals must be joined manually in Redshift — no automated group P&L dashboard; variance analysis delayed by 2-3 days post-travel

l4_steps.name: Update RM Demand Forecasting Model with Actuals
l4_steps.input: Revenue variance report; actual load factor contribution from group block; group yield data
l4_steps.output: Updated demand coefficients in NRM forecasting model; group segment historical database entry
l4_steps.kpi: Model update completed within 10 business days post-travel; forecast accuracy improvement of ≥0.5% per cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM group booking actuals are not automatically tagged separately from retail bookings — group demand is blended into overall O&D forecasts, distorting unconstrained demand estimates and causing systematic over-forecasting on high-group-volume routes

l4_steps.name: Extract PNR data for upsell candidate pool
l4_steps.input: Confirmed bookings within 72-hour pre-departure window
l4_steps.output: Upsell candidate PNR list with cabin class, fare basis, and loyalty tier
l4_steps.kpi: Candidate pool coverage ≥95% of eligible bookings extracted
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PNR data exports can lag up to 15 min during peak schedule periods, narrowing the actionable upsell window for close-in departures

l4_steps.name: Score passengers using willingness-to-pay model
l4_steps.input: PNR list, historical upsell acceptance data, loyalty tier, booking channel
l4_steps.output: WTP score (0–100) and predicted upgrade revenue per passenger
l4_steps.kpi: WTP model accuracy ≥82% (lift vs. random baseline on holdout set)
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM WTP models trained on pre-COVID data can overestimate premium-cabin demand for leisure-heavy route clusters; requires quarterly recalibration

l4_steps.name: Check premium cabin inventory for upgrade availability
l4_steps.input: Flight departure date, cabin class inventory snapshot, current load factor by cabin
l4_steps.output: Available upgrade seats per cabin class per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Premium cabin upgrade seat availability query response time <2 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time seat availability from AltéaRM can conflict with GDS inventory counts when passive segments are not cancelled promptly, creating ghost-availability errors

l4_steps.name: Segment eligible passengers by WTP tier and route
l4_steps.input: WTP scores, available upgrade inventory, route premium demand index
l4_steps.output: Prioritised upsell target list segmented into High / Medium / Low WTP tiers
l4_steps.kpi: High-WTP tier (score ≥70) constitutes ≥30% of total candidate pool
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty programme members in lower fare classes are frequently misclassified as low-WTP due to sparse ancillary purchase history in PROS RM

l4_steps.name: Generate dynamic upgrade offer price per passenger
l4_steps.input: WTP score, fare differential (booked fare vs. premium cabin fare), route load factor
l4_steps.output: Personalised upgrade offer price in local currency
l4_steps.kpi: Average upgrade offer price within 15% of O&D revenue maximisation model output
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM dynamic pricing engine does not natively ingest competitor same-day premium fare data, requiring manual competitive adjustment for price-sensitive O&D markets

l4_steps.name: Apply ATPCO fare floor and ceiling constraints
l4_steps.input: Generated offer price, filed fare rules (Rule 010 / 015), minimum fare differentials
l4_steps.output: Validated upgrade offer price compliant with ATPCO fare rules
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of published upgrade offers compliant with ATPCO Cat 25 negotiated fare rules
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 25 rule interpretation varies across PSS implementations; non-compliant upgrade offers can trigger GDS mis-pricing alerts and require emergency fare recall

l4_steps.name: Bundle ancillary services with upgrade offer
l4_steps.input: Validated upgrade price, ancillary catalogue (lounge, extra baggage, priority boarding)
l4_steps.output: Bundled upsell offer package with itemised ancillary pricing
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary attach rate per upgrade offer ≥40% on applicable routes
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway bundle assembly fails when ancillary inventory systems (lounge access, seat maps) return timeout errors, forcing fallback to offer-only pricing with no bundle

l4_steps.name: Publish upgrade offers via web check-in and mobile app
l4_steps.input: Bundled upgrade offer packages, passenger contact details from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Live upsell offer presented in web check-in and airline mobile app
l4_steps.kpi: Offer display latency <3 sec for ≥98% of web check-in sessions
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API retries during high-volume check-in peaks (T-24h departure) cause duplicate offer display or blank offer panels, degrading conversion rate

l4_steps.name: Send targeted upsell email and push notifications
l4_steps.input: Segmented passenger list with personalised offer price, departure T-48h and T-24h triggers
l4_steps.output: Email and push notification delivered with personalised upgrade CTA
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥28%; push notification click-through rate ≥12%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa CRM notification engine does not suppress duplicate messages when passengers have both web and mobile sessions active, leading to over-communication complaints

l4_steps.name: Display upgrade prompts at airport check-in and kiosk
l4_steps.input: Passenger check-in event, remaining upgrade inventory from AltéaRM
l4_steps.output: Upgrade upsell prompt displayed to agent and self-service kiosk
l4_steps.kpi: Airport upgrade conversion rate ≥8% of prompted passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS kiosk software version lag (often 2+ major releases behind) causes offer display failures on older kiosk hardware at smaller outstations

l4_steps.name: Process upgrade payment via preferred channel
l4_steps.input: Passenger acceptance of upgrade offer, payment card or loyalty points balance
l4_steps.output: Payment transaction record; EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) issued
l4_steps.kpi: Payment processing success rate ≥98.5%; transaction time <10 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa EMD issuance for upgrade payments using loyalty currency (miles + cash) requires manual fare recalculation when the loyalty system API returns stale balance data

l4_steps.name: Reassign seat and update PNR cabin class
l4_steps.input: Authorised payment confirmation, available premium cabin seat map
l4_steps.output: PNR updated with new cabin class, seat assignment, and fare basis code
l4_steps.kpi: PNR update latency <5 sec; zero duplicate seat assignment errors per 10,000 upgrades
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent upgrade processing for the same flight can cause seat-map race conditions in Altéa when two agents process the last available premium seat simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Provision premium cabin services and lounge access
l4_steps.input: Updated PNR with premium cabin indicator, lounge contract entitlements
l4_steps.output: Lounge access pass issued; premium meal and amenity kit flagged for catering
l4_steps.kpi: Premium service provisioning lead time ≥45 min before departure for ≥95% of upgrades
l4_steps.pain_point: Catering uplift amendments post-upgrade are frequently missed when the upgrade is processed inside the catering finality window (T-2h), resulting in insufficient premium meals

l4_steps.name: Send upgrade confirmation and boarding pass to passenger
l4_steps.input: PNR update complete, new boarding pass data, passenger email / mobile
l4_steps.output: Updated boarding pass (mobile and printable) and upgrade confirmation email
l4_steps.kpi: Confirmation delivery within 60 sec of PNR update for ≥99% of upgrades
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile boarding pass push fails for passengers using third-party wallet apps (non-Apple/Google Wallet) when Altéa PKPass API returns certificate validation errors

l4_steps.name: Aggregate upsell revenue and conversion metrics
l4_steps.input: EMD transaction records, PNR cabin upgrade events, offer impression logs
l4_steps.output: Daily upsell revenue report: impressions, conversions, revenue per upgrade, channel mix
l4_steps.kpi: Upsell revenue per available seat ≥$12 on applicable routes; daily report SLA <6h after day-end
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD revenue attribution in AWS Redshift is delayed by up to 4h due to batch ingestion from Altéa, preventing same-day intra-day optimisation of pricing parameters

l4_steps.name: Compare actuals vs. forecast upsell revenue targets
l4_steps.input: Daily upsell revenue report, budgeted upsell revenue targets by route cluster
l4_steps.output: Variance report: actual vs. forecast with root-cause flags (pricing, inventory, channel)
l4_steps.kpi: Upsell revenue forecast accuracy within ±10% of actuals on rolling 7-day basis
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pulling from AWS Redshift frequently timeout on full-network route-cluster queries, forcing analysts to run ad-hoc SQL instead of using governed reports

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate WTP model and pricing parameters
l4_steps.input: Variance report, offer acceptance/rejection data, competitor fare changes from OAG
l4_steps.output: Updated WTP model weights; revised pricing floor and ceiling parameters in PROS RM
l4_steps.kpi: WTP model recalibration cycle ≤7 days after conversion target miss; post-recalibration lift ≥5%
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM model retraining requires a minimum 90-day historical acceptance dataset; insufficient data on new routes or post-schedule-change periods degrades model quality for at least one quarter

l4_steps.name: Benchmark ancillary revenue vs. peer carriers
l4_steps.input: IATA annual ancillary revenue survey, peer carrier 10-K filings
l4_steps.output: Ancillary benchmark report with gap analysis by product category
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue per passenger ≥ $35 (IATA LCC benchmark); report produced annually
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA benchmark data lags 12–18 months; ultra-LCC peers (Spirit, Frontier) distort averages, masking true FSC comparison group and overstating apparent gap

l4_steps.name: Analyse ancillary product mix by revenue category
l4_steps.input: Amadeus Altéa PSS booking records, ancillary sales transaction log
l4_steps.output: Ancillary revenue decomposition: baggage, seat selection, F&B, insurance, partner referrals
l4_steps.kpi: Top-3 categories contribute ≥70% of total ancillary revenue; data refresh ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS ancillary sales codes are inconsistently applied by airport agents, causing product misclassification in Redshift that distorts category-level P&L

l4_steps.name: Identify new ancillary product opportunities
l4_steps.input: Benchmark gap analysis, passenger demand segmentation, route O&D traffic data
l4_steps.output: Ancillary product roadmap with prioritised opportunities and revenue potential estimates
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum 3 new ancillary product candidates identified per annual review cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D segmentation is designed for seat demand forecasting, not ancillary willingness-to-pay; proxy metrics must substitute for direct demand estimation, reducing confidence

l4_steps.name: Configure ancillary service catalog in PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved ancillary product roadmap, IATA EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) standards
l4_steps.output: Active ancillary service catalog with SSR/OSI codes and EMD settlement rules configured
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of approved ancillaries configured and testable in Altéa within 5 business days of sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD issuance rules require coordination with Finance for BSP settlement alignment; misconfigured EMD types generate revenue accounting errors and trigger BSP dispute processes

l4_steps.name: Set dynamic pricing rules for seats and baggage
l4_steps.input: Historical ancillary demand elasticity data, booking curve by flight, load factor thresholds
l4_steps.output: Dynamic ancillary price ladders by product, route, and days-to-departure bucket
l4_steps.kpi: Elasticity model coverage ≥80% of O&D pairs; yield uplift ≥8% vs. static pricing baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM dynamic ancillary pricing requires separate model training from core RM; data sparsity on thin routes produces unreliable elasticity estimates, defaulting to static fallback pricing

l4_steps.name: Design fare family bundles with ancillary inclusions
l4_steps.input: Fare family structure, ancillary cost-to-serve data, competitive bundle benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Defined fare family tiers (e.g. Basic / Standard / Flex) with ancillary inclusion matrix filed in ATPCO
l4_steps.kpi: Bundle attach rate ≥40% of total bookings; bundle margin ≥ à la carte revenue equivalent
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 15 (Sales Restrictions) and Category 31 (Voluntary Changes) rules must be manually aligned with each bundle tier — a mismatch causes GDS display failures and customer refund claims

l4_steps.name: Validate ancillary offers in NDC API test environment
l4_steps.input: Configured ancillary catalog, fare family bundle definitions from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: Validated NDC offer schema with ancillaries returned in AirShopping and OrderCreate responses
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ancillary products surfaced in NDC AirShopping response; NDC API error rate < 0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA NDC 21.3 schema requires ancillaries as ServiceDefinitionID objects; legacy Altéa ancillary codes must be manually mapped — mappings break on Altéa version upgrades requiring re-validation

l4_steps.name: Segment passengers for targeted ancillary offers
l4_steps.input: Loyalty programme profiles, booking history, route type (leisure/business), fare class
l4_steps.output: Passenger micro-segments with propensity scores for each ancillary product category
l4_steps.kpi: Propensity model AUC ≥0.72 for top-3 ancillary categories; segments refreshed ≤24 hours before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty data is siloed from GDS bookings — indirect-channel passengers have sparse profiles, reducing propensity model accuracy for ~35% of bookings and defaulting to generic offers

l4_steps.name: Configure real-time ancillary offer engine
